definition_zh: 许多的；许多（人或物）；许多（后接单数名词）；多数人；大众
definition_en: a large number of countable things; used as a pronoun for a large group; in the pattern many a with a singular noun; and the many as the ordinary majority
core_image: 广场上站满了人，一眼望去数不清有多少张脸
scene: 雨刚停，剧场门口的人已经排成长队，伞还在滴水。By the time the doors opened, many people had already been waiting for hours.
sceneCN: 这里指数目很多的人（第 1 个义项：许多的）；句意为开门时已经有许多人等了几个小时。

derivatives.zh: 由 many 与后缀 -fold（倍）复合，义为「许多倍的；成倍地」
由 many 与 sided 复合，义为「多方面的；多边的」
由 many-sided 加 -ness 构成，义为「多面性」

senses.title: A large number of countable things
senses.definition: used before a plural countable noun to say that the number of things or people is large
senses.definitionCN: 用在可数名词复数前，表示人或物的数目很大
senses.example: Many students walk to the library after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 许多学生午饭后步行去图书馆。
senses.why: Old English manig was already an adjective of quantity used with plurals, so the first job of the word is simply to put a large count in front of a noun.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 manig 本来就是与复数连用的数量形容词，所以这个词最初的工作，就是把一个很大的数目放在名词前面。

senses.title: A large number already mentioned
senses.definition: used as a pronoun, usually with of, for a large number of people or things that the listener can identify
senses.definitionCN: 作代词使用，常与 of 连用，指听者能够识别的一大群人或物
senses.example: Many of the old houses were built by the same family.
senses.exampleCN: 这些老房子有许多是同一家人建的。
senses.why: When the noun is dropped, the quantity word has to stand on its own, and of supplies the group it counts; the hearer fills in the rest from context.
senses.whyCN: 名词被省掉后，这个数量词只能自己站住，而 of 引出它所清点的群体；其余部分由听者根据上下文补足。

senses.title: Many a followed by a singular noun
senses.definition: a formal or literary pattern in which many a is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb, though the meaning is a large number
senses.definitionCN: 正式或文学性的结构：many a 后接单数名词与单数动词，但表达的是「许多」
senses.example: Many a sailor has told the same story about that storm.
senses.exampleCN: 许多水手都讲过关于那场风暴的同一个故事。
senses.why: The pattern counts one member at a time, which is why the noun and verb stay singular, yet the repetition adds up to a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 这个结构一次只点一个成员，所以名词和动词都用单数；但一次次相加，最后仍是一个群体。

senses.title: The many as the ordinary majority
senses.definition: the large group of ordinary people, especially when set against a small group with power or wealth
senses.definitionCN: 普通人的大多数，尤指与掌握权力或财富的少数群体相对时
senses.example: The policy was praised by the few and ignored by the many.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策得到少数人称赞，却被多数人忽视。
senses.why: With the definite article, many stops being a count and becomes a name for a social body, the crowd that stands opposite the few.
senses.whyCN: 带上定冠词之后，many 不再清点数量，而成为对一个社会群体的称呼：与少数人相对的众人。

intro.en: Many is a Germanic quantity adjective that has stayed close to its Old English form and keeps company with German manch and Dutch menig.
intro.cn: many 是日耳曼语的数量形容词，形态与古英语时期相距不远，并与德语 manch、荷兰语 menig 同属一族。

items.en: The word appears as manig or monig, an adjective of quantity meaning many or much, used with plural nouns.
items.cn: 这个词写作 manig 或 monig，是表示数量的形容词，意为许多、大量，与复数名词连用。

items.en: The reconstructed adjective *managaz is the common source of the English, German and Dutch forms.
items.cn: 重构形容词 *managaz 是英语、德语与荷兰语诸形式的共同来源。

items.en: Old Norse margr and German manch are cousins, which shows the word was a shared Germanic way of counting a crowd.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 margr 与德语 manch 是近亲，说明这个词是日耳曼语各支共有的清点人群的说法。

items.en: Middle English kept many for plural count nouns and paired it with much for masses, fixing the countable and uncountable split.
items.cn: 中古英语让 many 专管可数名词复数，与管不可数量的 much 配对，固定了可数与不可数的分工。

items.en: Modern English adds the pronoun use with of, the formal pattern many a, and the noun phrase the many for the ordinary majority.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了与 of 连用的代词用法、正式的 many a 结构，以及指普通大众的名词短语 the many。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic adjective of quantity whose form changed little, and whose grammar splits countable things from masses and from fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是形态变化很小的日耳曼语数量形容词，它的语法把可数事物、不可数总量和固定短语区分开来。

normal.en: Old English manig is the direct ancestor of many, and its -ig ending is the old adjective suffix for having a quality.
normal.cn: 古英语 manig 是 many 的直接祖先，其中的 -ig 词尾就是表示「具有某种性质」的古老形容词后缀。

normal.en: German manch and Dutch menig are cousins of many, which shows the word has been a Germanic quantity term all along.
normal.cn: 德语 manch 与荷兰语 menig 是 many 的近亲，说明这个词一直是日耳曼语的数量词。

normal.en: Many counts separate items and much measures a mass, so the two words divide the countable from the uncountable.
normal.cn: many 清点一件件分开的东西，much 衡量一团总量，两个词由此把可数与不可数分开。

normal.en: More and most are shared with much, which is why many never takes -er or -est.
normal.cn: more 与 most 是和 much 共用的，所以 many 从不加 -er 或 -est。

normal.en: Many a is followed by a singular noun and verb, while many alone takes a plural; the grammar marks the fixed pattern off from ordinary counting.
normal.cn: many a 后接单数名词与单数动词，而单独的 many 接复数；语法把这个固定结构与普通清点区分开来。

abstract.en: A crowd too dense to count is the simplest picture of many: the word begins with the failure of one-by-one counting.
abstract.cn: 一片多到数不清的人群，就是 many 最简单的画面：这个词从「没法一个个数」开始。

abstract.en: Saying many rather than much is a decision about how the world is sliced, into separate things or into a mass.
abstract.cn: 说 many 而不是 much，是在决定世界怎样被切开：切成一件件东西，还是看成一团总量。

abstract.en: The many and the few turn a number word into a picture of society, where counting becomes a question of who holds power.
abstract.cn: the many 与 the few 把一个数词变成社会图景，清点由此变成「谁掌握权力」的问题。

definition_zh: 三月；行军；齐步走；游行；进行曲；边界地区
definition_en: the third month of the year; to walk with regular steps like a soldier; an organized public protest; music written to keep marchers in step; and a border region
core_image: 一队人踩着同一个节拍前进，靴声连成一条线
scene: 冬夜还没过去，营房外的霜结在靴面上，远处的号声在空地上响起。The soldiers began to march before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里指列队齐步前进（第 2 个义项：行军）；句意为士兵们在黎明前开始行军。

senses.title: The third month of the year
senses.definition: the third month of the calendar year, falling at the start of spring in the northern hemisphere
senses.definitionCN: 公历一年中的第三个月，在北半球正值春天开始
senses.example: The first flowers usually appear here in March.
senses.exampleCN: 这里最早的花通常在三月出现。
senses.why: The month is named after Mars, the Roman god of war, and it opened the old Roman year, when armies set out again after winter; the war god thus stands at the head of the calendar.
senses.whyCN: 这个月以罗马战神玛尔斯命名，又是古罗马旧历的第一个月，军队在冬天之后重新出征；战神就这样站在日历的开端。

senses.title: To walk with a regular measured step
senses.definition: to walk with regular, measured steps, especially as part of a group of soldiers or a drilled body of people
senses.definitionCN: 以整齐、有节拍的步子行走，尤指作为士兵或受过操练的一群人中的一员
senses.example: The recruits learned to march in step before they were issued rifles.
senses.exampleCN: 新兵在领到步枪之前先学会了齐步走。
senses.why: Old French marchier meant to tramp along on foot, and military drill turned that heavy walking into a shared beat that a whole column could hold.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 marchier 意为徒步跋涉，军事操练把这种沉重的走法变成整支队伍都能保持的共同节拍。

senses.title: An organized public protest by walking
senses.definition: a public event in which a large group walks together through streets to express support for or opposition to something
senses.definitionCN: 一大群人一起走过街道、以表达支持或反对的公开活动
senses.example: Thousands joined the protest march through the city centre.
senses.exampleCN: 数千人参加了穿过市中心的抗议游行。
senses.why: A crowd on the move uses the soldier's rhythm for a civilian purpose: bodies side by side make a claim that is hard to ignore.
senses.whyCN: 移动中的一群人借用了士兵的节奏，却用于平民的目的：并排的身体提出一种难以忽视的主张。

senses.title: Music written for marching
senses.definition: a piece of music with a strong regular beat, written to accompany a group marching
senses.definitionCN: 节拍强劲而规整、用来伴随一群人行进的乐曲
senses.example: The band played a slow march as the veterans walked past.
senses.exampleCN: 老兵走过时，乐队奏起一支缓慢的进行曲。
senses.why: A march is named after the walk it controls, because its beat exists to keep boots landing together.
senses.whyCN: 进行曲以它所指挥的行走命名，因为它的节拍存在的目的，就是让靴子同时落地。

senses.title: A border region between two countries
senses.definition: a border area, especially one once contested between two kingdoms or peoples
senses.definitionCN: 边境地带，尤指两个王国或民族之间曾经争夺的地区
senses.example: The old castles along the Welsh marches were built to guard the frontier.
senses.exampleCN: 威尔士边境上的那些古堡是为守卫边界而建的。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different word, Old French marche, meaning a boundary; English spelled it like the walking word, and troops guarding a frontier kept the two meanings close.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个词——古法语 marche，意为边界；英语把它拼得和「行走」那个词一样，而驻守边境的军队让两个意思彼此靠近。

intro.en: March is two histories under one spelling: a Latin month name from the war god, and a French and Germanic group of words for walking and for a boundary.
intro.cn: march 是同一拼写下的两段历史：一段是来自战神的拉丁月份名，另一段是来自法语与日耳曼语、表示行走与边界的词族。

items.en: The month name comes from Martius, the adjective of Mars, the Roman god of war; it was the first month of the old Roman calendar.
items.cn: 月份名来自 Martius，即罗马战神玛尔斯的相关形容词；它是古罗马旧历的第一个月。

items.en: The walking verb is recorded in Old French as marchier, meaning to tramp or walk, and it passed into English as march.
items.cn: 表示行走的动词在古法语中记作 marchier，意为跋涉、步行，进入英语后成为 march。

items.en: The origin of marchier is usually traced to a reconstructed Frankish verb such as *markōn, though the exact form and sense are uncertain.
items.cn: marchier 的来源一般认为可追溯到重构的法兰克语动词（如 *markōn），但确切形式与含义并不确定。

items.en: The border sense comes from a separate Old French noun marche, a boundary or frontier, inherited from a Germanic word for a border.
items.cn: 边界义来自另一个古法语名词 marche，意为边界、边境，承自日耳曼语中表示边界的词。

items.en: Modern English keeps the month, the measured walk, the protest, the music and the border under one spelling, though the month and the border have separate histories.
items.cn: 现代英语把月份、齐步行走、游行、进行曲和边界都收在同一种拼写之下，尽管月份与边界各有来历。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the walking word and its Latin month root; the near-meaning group gathers words for organized group movement.
note.cn: 形近组收由「行走」这个词及其拉丁月份词根构成的形式；近义组收表示有组织群体移动的词。

entries.definition: Connected with war or soldiers, from the Latin adjective for Mars.
entries.definitionCN: 与战争或军人有关的，出自玛尔斯的拉丁形容词。

entries.definition: A person who marches, especially in a protest.
entries.definitionCN: 行进的人，尤指参加游行的人。

entries.definition: The act of walking in step, or a description of such a group.
entries.definitionCN: 齐步行进的动作，或用来形容这样一群人。

entries.definition: A formal parade in which troops march past a reviewing stand.
entries.definitionCN: 部队列队走过检阅台的正式分列式。

entries.definition: A public procession, often with marching and music.
entries.definitionCN: 公开的队列行进，常有齐步走和音乐。

entries.definition: A public gathering or march showing support or opposition.
entries.definitionCN: 表达支持或反对的公开集会或游行。

entries.definition: A line of people or vehicles moving forward in order.
entries.definitionCN: 人或车辆按顺序前进的队伍。

entries.definition: To walk with long steps at a steady pace.
entries.definitionCN: 以稳定的节奏迈大步走。

normalIntro.en: The word carries a calendar month, a measured step, a protest, a tune and a frontier, and only the spelling makes them look like one family.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词同时装着日历上的月份、有节拍的步伐、游行、曲子和边境，只有拼写让它们看起来像一家人。

normal.en: March the month and march the walk share a spelling but not a source: the month comes from Latin Martius, the walk from Old French marchier.
normal.cn: 表示月份的 March 与表示行走的 march 共享拼写却不共享来源：月份来自拉丁语 Martius，行走来自古法语 marchier。

normal.en: The month was named for Mars, and it was the first month of the old Roman year, which is why the war god's name opens the calendar.
normal.cn: 这个月以玛尔斯命名，又是古罗马旧历的第一个月，所以战神的名字站在日历的开端。

normal.en: Marchier meant to tramp on foot, and drill sharpened that walk into the measured step called marching.
normal.cn: marchier 意为徒步跋涉，操练把这种走法磨成了被称为 marching 的有节拍的步伐。

normal.en: The border sense is a third line, Old French marche, a boundary; only the spelling makes it look like the walking word.
normal.cn: 边界义是第三条线索，即古法语 marche（边界）；只有拼写让它看起来像「行走」那个词。

normal.en: March as music is named after the walk it governs, since its beat tells the feet when to land.
normal.cn: 作为音乐的 march 以它所指挥的行走命名，因为它的节拍告诉脚步何时落地。

abstract.en: A line of boots hitting the ground at one instant is the whole word in miniature: many bodies, one beat.
abstract.cn: 一排靴子在同一瞬间落地，就是这个词的缩影：许多身体，一个节拍。

abstract.en: The month and the walk meet at the war god, because spring was when armies moved again.
abstract.cn: 月份与行走在战神那里相遇，因为春天正是军队重新开动的时节。

abstract.en: A word can hold a calendar, a crowd, a tune and a frontier, and the spelling hides the fact that they come from different roads.
abstract.cn: 一个词可以同时装着日历、人群、曲子和边境，而拼写掩盖了它们来自不同道路这一事实。

examples.en: The soldiers began to march before dawn.
examples.cn: 士兵们在黎明前开始行军。

examples.en: Thousands joined the protest march through the city centre.
examples.cn: 数千人参加了穿过市中心的抗议游行。

examples.en: A brass band played a march as the column moved forward.
examples.cn: 队伍前进时，一支铜管乐队奏起进行曲。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马奇」——马奇带着队伍踏着整齐步伐前进；记住 march 是行军、游行。

root: 三月义来自拉丁语 Martius（战神玛尔斯之月）；行军、游行义来自古法语 marchier（跋涉、步行），其来源一般认为与法兰克语有关，具体形式不确定；边界义来自古法语 marche（边界），源自日耳曼语。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a body of people moving in one rhythm; the month comes from the war god who opens spring, the verb and the protest from organized walking, the music from the beat that keeps the walk together, and the border sense from a separate Old French word for a boundary.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是一群人按同一个节拍移动；月份来自开启春天的战神，动词与游行来自有组织的行走，进行曲来自维系步伐的节拍，边界义则来自另一个表示边界的古法语词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column of people stepping in time, boots striking one line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人踩着同一个节拍前进，靴声连成一条线。

branches.en: a calendar page bearing the war god's name
branches.cn: 印着战神名字的日历页

branches.en: boots striking the road in one rhythm
branches.cn: 靴子以同一种节拍踏在路面上

branches.en: a crowd with banners moving down a wide street
branches.cn: 举着横幅的人群走过宽阔的街道

branches.en: a brass band keeping a column in step
branches.cn: 铜管乐队让队列保持步调

branches.en: a stone castle watching a frontier
branches.cn: 一座古堡守望边境

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin month name, a French walking verb, a Germanic boundary noun, and English endings that name the people and the action.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁月份名、法语行走动词、日耳曼语边界名词，以及命名人物与动作的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Only the month sense has a Latin source: Martius, the month of Mars; the walking and border senses come from French and Germanic words.
latinIntro.cn: 只有月份义有拉丁语来源：Martius，即玛尔斯之月；行走义与边界义则来自法语和日耳曼语词。

definition_zh: 边缘；页边空白；差额；余地；利润空间；保证金
definition_en: the edge of an area, the blank space around printed text, the amount by which one thing differs from another, or the spare room kept for safety or profit
core_image: 纸页四周留出的白边：文字被围在中央，四周空着，可以写批注，也可以留作退路
scene: 编辑把校样摊在桌上。She wrote a note in red in the right margin, asking the author to delete a repeated sentence.
sceneCN: 这里 margin 是「页边空白」（第 2 个义项：书页文字四周的空白）；句意：她在右侧页边空白处用红笔写下一行批注，请作者删去重复的句子。图中可辨识物件：校样纸、红色批注、页边白区、钢笔；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: The edge of a physical area
senses.definition: the outer edge or border of a sea, lake, forest, field, or other area
senses.definitionCN: 海、湖、森林、田野或其他区域的外缘或边界
senses.example: Tall reeds grow along the margin of the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 高高的芦苇长在湖的边缘。
senses.why: Margin is first recorded in the mid-14c. as 'edge of a sea or lake'. Latin margo meant 'edge, brink, border', so the word starts at the outermost line where one area stops and another begins.
senses.whyCN: margin 最早记录于 14 世纪中期，意为“海或湖的边缘”。拉丁语 margo 意为“边缘、崖边、边界”，因此这个词的起点是一个区域终止、另一个区域开始的那条最外线。

senses.title: The blank space around a page of text
senses.definition: the blank space between a block of text and the edge of a page
senses.definitionCN: 一块文字与纸张边缘之间的空白区域
senses.example: She wrote questions in the margin beside each paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 她在每段旁边的页边空白处写下问题。
senses.why: By the late 14c. the word was used for the space between text and the edge of a leaf or sheet. The margin is not where writing ends but the reserved emptiness around it, which is why notes can later be added there.
senses.whyCN: 到 14 世纪晚期，这个词已用于指文字与纸页边缘之间的空间。页边不是文字结束的地方，而是文字周围被预留的空白，因此后来可以在那里加批注。

senses.title: The gap that decides a contest
senses.definition: the amount by which one competitor, result, or number is greater or smaller than another
senses.definitionCN: 一个竞争者、结果或数字比另一个大或小的量
senses.example: The bill passed by a margin of three votes.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法案以三票的差距通过。
senses.why: Two results sit side by side, and the margin is the strip of space between them. A narrow margin means the strip is thin, so the outcome could easily have gone the other way.
senses.whyCN: 两个结果并排放着，margin 就是两者之间那条空隙。narrow margin 意味着这条缝隙很窄，所以结果很容易倒向另一边。

senses.title: Spare room kept for safety
senses.definition: an amount of time, money, or tolerance kept free so that unexpected problems can be absorbed
senses.definitionCN: 预留出的时间、金钱或容差，用来吸收意外问题
senses.example: Leave a margin of ten minutes before the connecting train.
senses.exampleCN: 给换乘列车留出十分钟的余量。
senses.why: The sense 'comfort allowance, cushion, scope, provision for extended action' is recorded by 1851, and margin of error by 1889. A page margin protects the text; a safety margin protects the plan.
senses.whyCN: “舒适的余量、缓冲、活动空间、为扩大行动所作的预留”这一义项记录于 1851 年，margin of error 记录于 1889 年。页边保护文字，安全余量保护计划。

senses.title: The strip between cost and price
senses.titleCN: 成本与售价之间的那一条
senses.definition: the difference between the cost of producing or buying something and the price at which it is sold
senses.definitionCN: 生产或购买某物的成本与售价之间的差额
senses.example: The bakery survives on a thin profit margin.
senses.exampleCN: 这家面包店靠很薄的利润空间维持。
senses.why: In business the two sides of the page become cost and price, and the margin is the space between them. A thin margin leaves little room for error, which connects the financial sense back to the safety sense.
senses.whyCN: 在商业里，纸页的两边变成成本与售价，margin 就是两者之间的空间。薄利意味着几乎没有犯错的余地，这把金融义重新连回“安全余量”义。

senses.title: Collateral deposited with a broker
senses.definition: money deposited with a broker to cover the risk of loss when buying securities or goods on credit
senses.definitionCN: 以保证金方式买证券或货物时，交给经纪人以覆盖亏损风险的钱
senses.example: He bought the shares on margin and had to add cash after the drop.
senses.exampleCN: 他以保证金买进股票，股价下跌后不得不追加现金。
senses.why: The stock-market sense is recorded from 1848. The deposit is a buffer placed between the trader and a possible loss, exactly like the blank space that keeps the text from the edge.
senses.whyCN: 股市义记录于 1848 年。这笔押金是放在交易者与可能亏损之间的缓冲，和把文字与纸边隔开的空白完全同构。

senses.title: The edge of society: unimportant position
senses.titleCN: 社会的边缘：不重要的位置
senses.definition: a position at the edge of a group or society, with little influence or recognition
senses.definitionCN: 处于群体或社会边缘的位置，影响力或受认可度很低
senses.example: The report focuses on families living on the margins of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告关注生活在城市边缘的家庭。
senses.why: A page has a centre and a margin, and a society can be imagined the same way. The adjective marginal, 'of little effect or importance', is recorded from 1887, so the spatial word becomes a social judgement.
senses.whyCN: 一页纸有中心也有页边，一个社会也可以被这样想象。形容词 marginal“影响很小、不重要”记录于 1887 年，于是空间词变成了社会判断。

senses.title: To write in the margin
senses.definition: to add notes in the margin of a page, or to provide something with a margin
senses.definitionCN: 在书页边缘添加批注，或给某物留出边
senses.example: The student margined every chapter with questions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个学生在每一章的页边都写满了问题。
senses.why: The verb appears c. 1600 as 'to furnish with marginal notes', and from 1715 as 'to furnish with a margin'. The place becomes an action: the blank strip is put to use.
senses.whyCN: 动词义约在 1600 年出现，意为“加页边注”，1715 年起又表示“给……留边”。地点变成了动作：那条空白被用起来了。

senses.title: Usage boundary: margin is not edge, profit, or leeway
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：margin 不等于 edge、profit 或 leeway
senses.definition: margin usually implies reserved or measured space, not a hard boundary; profit margin is a ratio, not the profit itself; margins in finance are collateral, not earnings
senses.definitionCN: margin 通常暗示被预留或被量出的空间，而不是硬边界；profit margin 是比率，不是利润本身；金融里的 margins 是保证金，不是收益
senses.example: The company's margin is thin, but its total profit is still large.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的利润率很薄，但利润总额仍然很大。
senses.why: Edge is simply where something stops; margin is the strip left around it. Profit is the money kept; a profit margin is the proportion that money represents. Keeping these apart prevents 'a large margin' from being read as 'a large profit'.
senses.whyCN: edge 只是某物终止的地方；margin 是围绕它留下的那一条。profit 是留下的钱；profit margin 是这笔钱所占的比例。分清这些，才不会把“a large margin”误读成“a large profit”。

intro.en: Margin began as the physical edge of water or land, then became the blank strip around printed text. From that strip came the ideas of a gap between results, spare room for safety, and the difference between cost and price.
intro.cn: margin 最初指水域或陆地的实体边缘，随后变成印刷文字四周的空白条。从这条空白又衍生出结果之间的差距、为安全预留的余量，以及成本与售价之间的差额。

items.en: First recorded as 'edge of a sea or lake', from Old French margin and directly from Latin marginem (nominative margo) 'edge, brink, border, margin'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“海或湖的边缘”，来自古法语 margin，并直接来自拉丁语 marginem（主格 margo）“边缘、崖边、边界、页边”。

items.en: The sense 'space between a block of text and the edge of a leaf or sheet' appears. The general sense 'bordering space, boundary space, rim or edge' follows in the same period.
items.cn: “文字块与纸页边缘之间的空间”义出现。“边界空间、边缘、外缘”的一般义也在同一时期出现。

items.en: margo is traced to PIE *merg- 'boundary, border'. The reconstruction is generally accepted; the root is also associated with mark and march, though those reach English by other routes.
items.cn: margo 被追溯到原始印欧语 *merg-“边界、边缘”。这一重构属于一般认为；该词根也与 mark、march 有关，但后两者经其他路径进入英语。

items.en: The stock-market sense 'sum deposited with a broker to cover risk of loss' is recorded from 1848, the earliest of the modern figurative senses.
items.cn: 股市义“交给经纪人以覆盖亏损风险的押金”记录于 1848 年，是现代引申义中最早的一个。

items.en: The sense 'comfort allowance, cushion, scope, range' is recorded by 1851, and margin of error by 1889. Marginal, 'of little effect or importance', follows in 1887.
items.cn: “舒适余量、缓冲、活动空间、范围”义记录于 1851 年，margin of error 记录于 1889 年。marginal“影响很小、不重要”随后于 1887 年出现。

items.en: Modern English keeps the page sense, adds profit margin and social margins, and keeps the verb meaning 'to annotate'. The core idea is always reserved space between two things.
items.cn: 现代英语保留页边义，增加利润率与社会边缘义，并保留动词“加旁注”义。核心始终是两样东西之间被预留的空间。

note.en: The first group is built on margo or the margin shape. The second group separates the physical edge, the dividing line, the financial gain and the freedom to act.
note.cn: 第一组建立在 margo 或 margin 词形上。第二组区分实体边缘、分界线、财务收益与行动自由。

entries.definition: written in a margin, at the edge, or too small to matter. It is the adjective from margin, recorded from the 1570s.
entries.definitionCN: 写在页边的、位于边缘的，或小到不重要的。它是 margin 的形容词，记录于 16 世纪 70 年代。

entries.definition: notes written in the margins of a book. It is the plural of the Latin neuter marginalis.
entries.definitionCN: 写在书页边上的批注。它是拉丁语中性形式 marginalis 的复数。

entries.definition: a poetic or old-fashioned word for edge or margin. It is easily confused with margarine, which is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 诗歌或旧式用语中的“边缘”。它容易被误认成 margarine（人造黄油），后者与此无关。

entries.definition: the line where a surface ends. It is sharper and more literal than margin, which often implies a strip of reserved space.
entries.definitionCN: 一个表面终止的那条线。它比 margin 更锋利、更字面；margin 常暗示一条被预留的空间。

entries.definition: the line dividing two countries or regions. It is political or geographic, while margin is usually a space rather than a line.
entries.definitionCN: 分隔两国或两地区的界线。它是政治或地理的；margin 通常是空间，而不是一条线。

entries.definition: the money left after costs are paid. A profit margin is the ratio, not the sum, so the two are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 付完成本后剩下的钱。profit margin 是比率而不是金额，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: the freedom to act or to be late without punishment. Margin is the spare amount; leeway is the permission to use it.
entries.definitionCN: 行动的自由，或可迟到而不受罚的宽容度。margin 是预留的量；leeway 是使用这个量的许可。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: margo 'edge' gives margin and marginal; the blank strip on a page is the image behind every later financial and social sense.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：margo“边缘”给出 margin 与 marginal；纸页上的空白条是后来所有金融义与社会义的底层意象。

normal.en: Look at a printed page: the text sits in the middle and a white strip runs around it. That strip is the margin, and every other sense is a version of it.
normal.cn: 看一页印刷纸：文字在中间，四周有一条白边。那条白边就是 margin，其他所有义项都是它的变体。

normal.en: A margin of error is a white strip around a measurement; buy on margin is a cash strip around a risky trade.
normal.cn: margin of error 是测量结果四周的白边；buy on margin 是一笔风险交易四周的现金缓冲。

normal.en: Profit margin is the strip between cost and price, thin or wide. It is a ratio, not the money itself.
normal.cn: profit margin 是成本与售价之间的那一条，可宽可窄。它是比率，不是钱本身。

normal.en: On the margins of society means at the edge of the page, outside the main text.
normal.cn: on the margins of society 就是处在纸页边缘、正文之外。

normal.en: The verb margin means writing in that strip: the place turns into an action.
normal.cn: 动词 margin 就是在那一条上写字：地点变成了动作。

abstract.en: Picture every important thing with a strip of empty space around it: a page, a score, a budget, a life. Margin is that strip, and its width tells you how safe or how thin things are.
abstract.cn: 想象每一件要紧的东西四周都留有一条空白：一页纸、一场比分、一份预算、一段人生。margin 就是那条空白，它的宽度告诉你事情有多安全、有多紧。

abstract.en: When the strip is inside a system it is tolerance; when it is inside a business it is profit; when it is inside a society it is exclusion.
abstract.cn: 当这条空白在系统内部，它是容差；在商业内部，它是利润；在社会内部，它是排斥。

abstract.en: The margin is never the centre, but nothing at the centre can be measured without it.
abstract.cn: 页边永远不是中心，但中心的一切都离不开它才能被量出来。

examples.en: The village sits at the margin of the forest and the marsh.
examples.cn: 这个村子位于森林与沼泽的边缘。

examples.en: The team won by a margin of two goals.
examples.cn: 这支球队以两球的差距获胜。

examples.en: Small shops survive on narrow margins and loyal customers.
examples.cn: 小店靠薄利和忠实顾客维持。

dict_mnemonic.text: “马诊”——马医生在页边空白处记下诊断，留出余地再下结论 → margin 页边、余地、差额

root: 拉丁语 margo（属格 marginis）“边缘、边界”，核心是“中心之外的那一条空间”，由页边引申为差额、余地、利润与保证金。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of margin, all one strip of reserved space: the edge of land, the blank page, a winning gap, a safety cushion, a profit ratio, broker's collateral, social periphery, a marginal note, and the boundary against edge and profit.
sensesIntro.cn: margin 的九个义项都是同一条被预留的空间：土地边缘、页边空白、胜负差距、安全余量、利润比率、经纪人保证金、社会边缘、页边批注，以及它与 edge、profit 的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strip of empty space runs between the centre and the outer limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条空白带介于中心与最外缘之间。

branches.en: LAND: the first sense is the physical rim where water, forest or field ends.
branches.cn: 土地：最早的义项是水域、森林或田野终止的实体外缘。

branches.en: PAGE: the blank strip around text, and the act of writing notes in it.
branches.cn: 纸页：文字四周的空白条，以及在其中写批注的动作。

branches.en: GAP: the measured space between two results is also the space kept free for safety.
branches.cn: 差距：两个结果之间被量出的空间，也是为安全而预留的空间。

branches.en: MONEY: cost and price leave a strip of profit; a broker holds a strip of collateral.
branches.cn: 金钱：成本与售价之间留下利润的那一条；经纪人手里握着保证金那一条。

branches.en: SOCIETY AND BOUNDARY: people at the edge of the page become marginal, and the strip is never a hard line.
branches.cn: 社会与边界：处在纸页边缘的人变成 marginal，而这条空白从不是一条硬线。

intro.en: Margin has no live English prefix. Its Latin stem margo, margin- is frozen inside; English adds -al, -ally, -alize and -alia to build the family.
intro.cn: margin 没有活的英语前缀。它的拉丁词干 margo、margin- 凝固在词内；英语加 -al、-ally、-alize、-alia 构成词族。

latinIntro.en: The *merg- 'boundary' root also underlies mark and march, which reached English through Germanic routes. Within English, the margin family is built on the Latin stem margin-.
latinIntro.cn: *merg-“边界”这个词根也支撑 mark 与 march，它们经日耳曼路径进入英语。在英语内部，margin 词族建立在拉丁词干 margin- 上。

items.meaning: written in a margin, situated at an edge, or small enough to be unimportant
items.meaningCN: 页边的；边缘的；微不足道的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The difference in cost is marginal.
items.exampleCN: 成本上的差别微不足道。

items.meaningCN: 略微；轻微地；在边缘地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The second design is marginally cheaper.
items.exampleCN: 第二个设计稍微便宜一点。

items.meaning: to push a person or group to the edge of influence
items.meaningCN: 使边缘化；把某人或群体排挤到影响力边缘（-ize 表示“使……化”）
items.example: Cheap transport marginalised the old market.
items.exampleCN: 廉价的交通让老市场边缘化了。

items.meaning: notes written in the margins of a book
items.meaningCN: 页边注；旁注（-ia 构成复数名词）
items.example: The library copy is full of marginalia.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆那本书上写满了旁注。

items.structure: Latin noun, third declension, genitive marginis
items.example: The noun is the direct source of margin.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是 margin 的直接来源。

items.example: The stem appears in margin, marginal and marginalia.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 margin、marginal 与 marginalia。

items.example: It forms marginal, belonging to the edge.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 marginal，即属于边缘的。

items.meaning: to make, to cause to be
items.example: It forms marginalize, to push to the edge.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 marginalize，即把……推向边缘。

items.example: It forms marginalia, notes written in the margins.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 marginalia，即写在页边的批注。

latinEntries.meaning: the act of marking a boundary

latinEntries.meaningCN: 标记；界标（原指边界记号）

latinEntries.meaning: borderland; the boundary region between two countries

latinEntries.structure: Old French marchis (lord of a march) from marche (border)
latinEntries.meaning: a noble ranking below a duke, originally the lord of a border region
latinEntries.meaningCN: 侯爵（原指边境地区的领主）

definition_zh: 海的；海洋的；海生的；航海的；（名词）海军陆战队员
definition_en: relating to the sea, living in the sea, or connected with shipping and naval forces; as a noun, a soldier trained to serve at sea and on coasts
core_image: 退潮后的礁池里，海藻贴着石面，小蟹在浅水里横着走
scene: 退潮后的礁石间满是海藻和小蟹，是一处微缩的海洋群落。Between the rocks at low tide lived seaweed and crabs, a marine community in miniature.
sceneCN: 这里 marine 指「海洋的、海生的」（第 2 个义项：生活在海中的生物群落）；句意：退潮后的礁石间住着海藻与小蟹，是一个微缩的海洋群落。图中可辨识物件：礁池、贴石的海藻、小蟹、退潮留下的水线；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 海的；海洋的；海生的；航海的；海军的
海军陆战队员；（大写)美国海军陆战队成员

forms.label: 复数名词（海军陆战队员）

senses.title: Of the sea as an environment
senses.titleCN: 海洋环境的、与海有关的
senses.definition: relating to the sea as a physical environment, including its water, floor and shores
senses.definitionCN: 与作为物理环境的海洋有关，包括海水、海底与海岸
senses.example: The marine environment absorbs a large share of human carbon emissions.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋环境吸收了人类碳排放的很大一部分。
senses.why: Latin mare means sea, so the adjective marks the sea as a setting for any process, not only for living things.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 mare 意为「海」，因此这个形容词标记海洋作为任何过程的场景，而不只用于生物。

senses.title: Living in the sea
senses.definition: describing plants and animals that live in salt water, especially in open sea habitats
senses.definitionCN: 描述生活在咸水中、尤指开阔海域生境的动植物
senses.example: Between the rocks at low tide lived seaweed and crabs, a marine community in miniature.
senses.exampleCN: 退潮后的礁石间住着海藻与小蟹，是一个微缩的海洋群落。
senses.why: the adjective attaches to the organism by its medium, and marine contrasts with freshwater and terrestrial.
senses.whyCN: 形容词按介质附着于生物，marine 与 freshwater、terrestrial 形成对照。

senses.title: Connected with shipping and seafaring
senses.definition: relating to ships, navigation and commerce by sea
senses.definitionCN: 与船舶、航行和海上贸易有关
senses.example: Marine insurance covers cargo lost overboard in heavy weather.
senses.exampleCN: 海运保险承保恶劣天气中落水的货物。
senses.why: sea transport is the oldest commercial use of the sea, so marine became the standard adjective in shipping and insurance law.
senses.whyCN: 海上运输是海洋最古老的商业用途，因此 marine 成为航运与保险法中的标准形容词。

senses.title: Naval and marine forces
senses.definition: relating to naval forces, especially soldiers trained to fight at sea or on coasts
senses.definitionCN: 与海军力量有关，尤指受训在海上或海岸作战的士兵
senses.example: Marine units were the first to reach the flooded port.
senses.exampleCN: 海军陆战队是最先抵达被淹港口的部队。
senses.why: the noun marine 'soldier serving at sea' arose because such troops belong to the sea service, so the adjective and the soldier share one form.
senses.whyCN: 名词 marine「在海上服役的士兵」之所以出现，是因为这类部队属于海上军种，因此形容词与士兵同名。

senses.title: Of the sea floor and its deposits
senses.definition: describing sediments, rocks and layers formed on or under the sea floor
senses.definitionCN: 描述在海底或海底之下形成的沉积物、岩石与层理
senses.example: Marine sediments record thousands of years of climate change.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋沉积物记录了几千年的气候变化。
senses.why: geology needed a term for deposits laid down by water, and marine specifies salt-water basins rather than lakes.
senses.whyCN: 地质学需要指「由水沉积」的术语，marine 则进一步限定为咸水盆地而非湖泊。

senses.title: Moderate climate influenced by the sea
senses.titleCN: 受海洋调节的（海洋性气候）
senses.definition: describing a climate with small temperature swings because the sea moderates the air above it
senses.definitionCN: 描述因海洋调节其上方空气而温差较小的气候
senses.example: The island's marine climate keeps winters mild and summers cool.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的海洋性气候使冬天温和、夏天凉爽。
senses.why: climatology applies the sea adjective to places whose weather is dominated by nearby water, in contrast with continental climates.
senses.whyCN: 气候学把「海」的形容词用于受近海支配的天气，与大陆性气候相对。

senses.title: Of marine science as a discipline
senses.definition: used for the scientific study of the sea, as in marine biology, marine chemistry and marine geology
senses.definitionCN: 用于海洋科学研究，如海洋生物学、海洋化学与海洋地质学
senses.example: The station runs a marine science programme for local schools.
senses.exampleCN: 该站为本地学校开设海洋科学课程。
senses.why: each sea-related discipline prefixed its name with marine, making the adjective a stable label for a whole field.
senses.whyCN: 各门与海有关的学科都在名称前加 marine，使该形容词成为整个领域的稳定标签。

senses.title: A soldier of the marine corps
senses.definition: a member of a military force trained for operations at sea, on coasts and in amphibious landings
senses.definitionCN: 受训执行海上、海岸与两栖登陆作战任务的军人
senses.example: Two marines guarded the gangway while the cargo was checked.
senses.exampleCN: 货物检查时，两名陆战队员守着舷梯。
senses.why: the noun is a shortened form of marine soldier, and it survives as the everyday name of the corps in several navies.
senses.whyCN: 该名词是 marine soldier 的缩略，至今仍是若干海军中这支兵种的日常称呼。

intro.en: Marine comes from Latin marinus 'of the sea', from mare 'sea'. English borrowed it through Old French in the fifteenth century, and the soldier sense followed in the seventeenth.
intro.cn: marine 来自拉丁 marinus「海的」，源于 mare「海」。英语经古法语在 15 世纪借入，士兵义在 17 世纪随后出现。

items.en: Mare was the ordinary Latin word for sea. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and the Indo-European form sometimes cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: mare 是拉丁语中表示「海」的常用词。其更深来源不确定，有时为其引用的印欧形式属重构。

items.en: Marinus 'of the sea' was formed from mare, and it described sea creatures, sea water and sea-going matters.
items.cn: marinus「海的」由 mare 构成，用于描述海洋生物、海水与航海事务。

items.en: Old French marin brought the adjective into English around 1400, first in natural history and then in shipping.
items.cn: 古法语 marin 在 15 世纪初把该形容词带入英语，最初见于博物学，随后进入航运。

items.en: In the seventeenth century marine was used as a noun for soldiers raised to serve aboard ships, the origin of the modern marine corps.
items.cn: 17 世纪，marine 用作名词，指招募到舰上服役的士兵，这是现代海军陆战队的源头。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century oceanography prefixed its subfields with marine, fixing the adjective in names such as marine biology and marine geology.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪的海洋学给各分支冠以 marine，使该形容词固定出现在 marine biology、marine geology 等名称中。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin history of mare is unsettled, and the earliest English citation is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：mare 在拉丁语之前的历史无定论，英语最早书证的年代也只能大致确定。

note.en: Group one distinguishes marine from same-root words for sailors, harbours and sea law, and from a look-alike with a different root; group two contrasts it with other sea-related adjectives.
note.cn: 第一组把 marine 与同根却指水手、码头、海事法的词区分开，并辨明一个词根不同的形近词；第二组对照其它与海有关的形容词。

entries.definition: A sailor; it comes from Latin marinarius through French, so it shares mare but names a person, not a habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 水手；经法语来自拉丁 marinarius，与 mare 同源，但指人而非生境。

entries.definition: A basin for pleasure boats; the -a ending makes it a place, while marine is the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 供游艇停泊的小港；-a 词尾使它指场所，而 marine 是形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to the sea in law, trade and defence; from Latin maritimus, it is the formal legal cousin of marine.
entries.definitionCN: 在法律、贸易与防务上与海有关的；来自拉丁 maritimus，是 marine 的正式法律近亲。

entries.definition: Relating to marriage; it comes from Latin maritus 'husband', not mare 'sea', so the resemblance is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 与婚姻有关的；来自拉丁 maritus「丈夫」而非 mare「海」，因此形近只是巧合。

entries.definition: Relating to the open ocean, especially far from coasts; marine is broader and includes shelves and shores.
entries.definitionCN: 与开阔大洋有关，尤指远离海岸；marine 范围更广，包含陆架与海岸。

entries.definition: Relating to a navy and its ships; marine covers civil and biological senses as well.
entries.definitionCN: 与海军及其舰船有关的；marine 还覆盖民用与生物义。

entries.definition: Relating to sailors, ships and navigation; it stresses seamanship rather than the sea itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与水手、船舶和航行有关的；它强调航海术而非海洋本身。

entries.definition: Describing salty water or organisms in it; it names the chemical condition that marine assumes.
entries.definitionCN: 描述咸水或其中的生物；它点明 marine 所预设的化学条件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real mare root, real derivatives and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 mare 词根、真实派生词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Mare is Latin for sea, and it survives in marine, mariner, marina and maritime.
normal.cn: mare 是拉丁语的「海」，仍见于 marine、mariner、marina、maritime。

normal.en: Marine life, marine ecosystem and marine biology are the standard biology collocations.
normal.cn: marine life、marine ecosystem、marine biology 是生物学的标准搭配。

normal.en: Marine insurance and marine law keep the shipping sense alive in legal English.
normal.cn: marine insurance 与 marine law 让航运义在法律英语中延续。

normal.en: The proper noun Marine Corps explains why a soldier is simply 'a marine'.
normal.cn: 专名 Marine Corps 解释了为什么士兵直接被称为 a marine。

normal.en: Marine climate is the climatology partner of continental climate.
normal.cn: marine climate 是大陆性气候在气候学中的配对词。

abstract.en: Picture a tide pool that holds an entire ocean's logic in a bowl of water.
abstract.cn: 想象一个潮池，用一盆水装下整片大洋的逻辑。

abstract.en: Picture a cargo crate whose insurance policy never leaves the shore.
abstract.cn: 想象一只货箱，它的保单从未离开海岸。

abstract.en: Picture a soldier trained on a beach, halfway between land and sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一名在海滩受训的士兵，站在陆地与海洋之间。

examples.en: Marine plastic debris accumulates in mid-ocean gyres.
examples.cn: 海洋塑料垃圾在洋流环流中积聚。

examples.en: The marine climate keeps the island green through winter.
examples.cn: 海洋性气候让这座岛整个冬天保持绿色。

examples.en: Marines secured the dock before the aid ships arrived.
examples.cn: 海军陆战队员在救援船到达前控制了码头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mare（海）+ ine」——mare 是海，marine 就是「海的、海里的」；大写 Marine 又一跃成了陆战队员

root: 拉丁 marinus「海的」= mare「海」+ -inus（形容词后缀）；mare 的更深来源不确定。英语 marine；同族有 mariner、maritime、marina。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one body of salt water: the sea as environment, the life in it, shipping, naval troops, sea-floor deposits, sea-moderated climate, marine science, and finally the soldier whose name is the noun form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一片咸水辐射开来：作为环境的海洋、其中的生命、海运、海军部队、海底沉积、受海调节的气候、海洋科学，最后是以名词形式出现的陆战队员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the salt sea as a place, a medium and a service.
core.cn: 核心意象：咸海既是场所，也是介质，也是服役对象。

branches.en: SEA AS HABITAT: the adjective marks both the setting and the organisms in it.
branches.cn: 海作为生境：形容词既标场景，也标其中的生物。

branches.en: SEA AS ROUTE: shipping and insurance turn the sea into infrastructure.
branches.cn: 海作为航线：航运与保险把海变成基础设施。

branches.en: SEA AS SERVICE: naval troops and the marine corps make the adjective a rank and a noun.
branches.cn: 海作为军务：海军部队与陆战队使形容词兼作军种名与名词。

branches.en: SEA AS OBJECT OF STUDY: sediments and marine science name what is examined.
branches.cn: 海作为研究对象：沉积物与海洋科学指出被考察之物。

branches.en: SEA AS CLIMATE FORCE: nearby water moderates the air above it.
branches.cn: 海作为气候力量：近旁的水调节其上方的空气。

intro.en: Marine is built on the Latin noun mare 'sea' plus -inus; the same root yields mariner, marina, maritime and the submarine, while sub- and mariculture extend it in modern technical words.
intro.cn: marine 由拉丁名词 mare「海」加 -inus 构成；同一词根衍生 mariner、marina、maritime 与 submarine，而 sub- 与 mariculture 在现代技术词中加以扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin mare 'sea', marinus 'of the sea' and maritimus 'of the coast' are the core ancestors of the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mare「海」、marinus「海的」与 maritimus「海岸的」是这一英语词族的核心祖形。

items.example: Marinus means belonging to the sea.

items.example: Marine algae anchor the coastal food web.

items.example: The marina sheltered twenty small boats.

definition_zh: 记号；痕迹；标记；符号；分数；留下痕迹；注意
definition_en: a small visible trace or spot; a written sign or symbol; a grade given for schoolwork; to leave a visible trace; to notice or pay attention to
core_image: 一支红笔在纸页角落画下一个小小的圈
scene: 海图摊在桌上，灯下的纸页已经发黄，边角还有折过的痕迹。A red mark on the chart showed where the ship had struck the reef.
sceneCN: 这里指留在纸面上的可见痕迹（第 1 个义项：记号、痕迹）；句意为海图上的一处红色记号标出了船撞上礁石的位置。

senses.title: A visible spot or line left on a surface
senses.definition: a small area of damage, colour or dirt that shows something has touched or pressed a surface
senses.definitionCN: 表面上一小块颜色、污迹或破损，显示有东西接触或压过
senses.example: A red mark on the chart showed where the ship had struck the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 海图上的一处红色记号标出了船撞上礁石的位置。
senses.why: Old English mearc first named a boundary sign, a visible thing set down to show where something is or has happened, and that visible trace is the core of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mearc 最初指边界的标志，是一件看得见的东西，用来说明某物在哪里或发生过什么；这种可见的痕迹就是这个词的核心。

senses.title: A written sign or symbol
senses.definition: a sign, symbol or written figure used to represent something or to give information
senses.definitionCN: 用来代表某物或提供信息的符号、记号或书写图样
senses.example: Put a mark beside the name of the candidate you prefer.
senses.exampleCN: 在你更中意的候选人名字旁边做一个标记。
senses.why: Once a visible sign can stand for something other than itself, the boundary trace becomes a symbol, and writing turns that symbol into a small reusable unit of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 当一件可见的标记能够代表它自身以外的东西，边界痕迹就变成符号，而文字又把这个符号变成可反复使用的小单位。

senses.title: A score or grade given for work
senses.definition: a number or letter showing how well a piece of schoolwork or a performance has been judged
senses.definitionCN: 表示某份作业或某次表现被评为多好的数字或字母
senses.example: She was pleased with the mark she received on the essay.
senses.exampleCN: 她对自己的作文分数很满意。
senses.why: A teacher's mark was once a physical sign placed next to an answer; because that sign recorded quality, the sign itself came to mean the judgement written into it.
senses.whyCN: 教师的 mark 原是画在答案旁边的一个实记号；正因为这个记号记录了优劣，记号本身便转而表示写在里面的评判。

senses.title: To leave a visible trace on something
senses.definition: to make a visible spot, line or sign on a surface, often to identify or record something
senses.definitionCN: 在表面上留下可见的点、线或符号，常用来识别或记录
senses.example: She marked the page with a folded corner before returning the book.
senses.exampleCN: 她折了个角给那一页做记号，然后才把书还回去。
senses.why: The verb is the noun put into action: to mark is to produce the very trace that the noun names, and the purpose is usually to make something findable later.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词化为动作：mark 某物，就是造出名词所指的那种痕迹，目的通常是让某样东西日后能被找到。

senses.title: To notice or pay attention to
senses.definition: to notice something and give it attention, especially because it deserves to be remembered
senses.definitionCN: 注意到某事并加以关注，尤因它值得被记住
senses.example: Mark my words: the second attempt will be harder than the first.
senses.exampleCN: 记住我的话：第二次尝试会比第一次更难。
senses.why: A mark draws the eye to one spot, so to mark something in speech is to single it out mentally and ask the listener to keep it in view.
senses.whyCN: 记号把目光引向某一处，所以在言语中说 mark 某事，就是在心里把它单独标出，并要求听者一直记着。

intro.en: Mark began as a Germanic word for a boundary sign, and from that visible sign it grew into a trace, a symbol, a grade and an act of attention.
intro.cn: mark 起初是日耳曼语中表示边界标志的词，从那个可见的标志出发，长出痕迹、符号、分数与注意等义。

items.en: The boundary sense is usually traced to a reconstructed root *merg-, meaning a border or edge, though the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 边界义一般认为可追溯到重构词根 *merg-，意为边界、边缘，但这一重构并不完全确定。

items.en: The reconstructed noun *markō meant a boundary and a sign set on it, and it is the base of the English word.
items.cn: 重构名词 *markō 意为边界以及立在边界上的标志，是英语这个词的词基。

items.en: Old English mearc covered a boundary, a landmark and a sign, so the word already joined the idea of an edge to the idea of something visible.
items.cn: 古英语 mearc 同时表示边界、地标和标志，这个词已经把「边缘」与「看得见的东西」连在一起。

items.en: Middle English mark widened to any trace, target or written symbol, and school use added the sense of a judgement written beside an answer.
items.cn: 中古英语 mark 扩展到任何痕迹、目标或书写符号，学校里的用法又增加了「写在答案旁边的评判」这一义。

items.en: Modern English adds the verb of noticing and the compounds marker, bookmark and trademark, while the border sense survives mainly in place names.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了表示「注意」的动词，以及 marker、bookmark、trademark 等复合词，边界义则主要留存在地名里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on mark and its old boundary root; the near-meaning group gathers words for signs, stains and grades.
note.cn: 形近组收由 mark 及其古老边界词根构成的形式；近义组收表示符号、污迹与分数的词。

entries.definition: Clearly noticeable, or having a mark on it.

entries.definition: An object or link used to keep a place in a book or on a page.

entries.definition: A comment; to say something about what one has noticed.

entries.definition: A symbol, notice or gesture that conveys information.

entries.definition: A mark or object that represents something else.

normalIntro.en: The word starts as a boundary sign cut into the ground, becomes any visible trace, and then any symbol, judgement or act of attention.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从刻在地面上的边界标志开始，先变成任何可见的痕迹，再变成符号、评判或注意的动作。

normal.en: Old English mearc meant a boundary and a sign, so the word began with something placed on the ground to show where one thing ends and another begins.
normal.cn: 古英语 mearc 意为边界与标志，所以这个词起初指放在地面上的东西，用来说明一物到何处为止、另一物从何处开始。

normal.en: The same old sense survives in the Welsh marches, a border region, and in the Latin relative margo, a margin or edge.
normal.cn: 同样的旧义留存在威尔士边境这一地名里，也留存在拉丁语近亲 margo（页边、边缘）中。

normal.en: A school mark began as a sign written beside an answer, and the sign came to stand for the judgement it recorded.
normal.cn: 学校的 mark 原是写在答案旁的记号，后来这个记号转而代表它所记录的评判。

normal.en: The verb mark is the noun turned into an action: the trace and the act of making it share one form.
normal.cn: 动词 mark 是名词化为动作：痕迹与留下痕迹的行为共用一种形式。

normal.en: Mark my words uses the physical sign as a mental one: the words are singled out so the listener will not forget them.
normal.cn: Mark my words 把实体的记号用作心里的记号：把话单独标出，让听者不会忘记。

abstract.en: A single red circle can point to a reef, a name or a mistake, because a mark is attention made visible.
abstract.cn: 一个小小的红圈可以指向礁石、名字或错误，因为记号就是被看见的注意。

abstract.en: A boundary and a symbol are the same gesture: something small is placed to say this is where meaning begins.
abstract.cn: 边界与符号是同一个动作：放下某件小小的东西，说「意义从这里开始」。

abstract.en: To mark a word in a book is to ask the page to remember for you.
abstract.cn: 在书里给一个词做记号，就是请纸页替你记住。

examples.en: A red mark on the chart showed where the ship had struck the reef.
examples.cn: 海图上的一处红色记号标出了船撞上礁石的位置。

examples.cn: 在你更中意的候选人名字旁边做一个标记。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a visible trace placed on a surface; the written symbol, the grade, the act of marking and the mental act of noticing all grow from that one visible sign.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是留在表面上的可见痕迹；书写符号、分数、做记号的动作以及心里的留意，都从这同一个可见标志长出。
