definition_zh: 市场；集市；某种商品的交易领域；销路、需求；股市；行销、推销
definition_en: a place or system in which goods and services are bought and sold, or the willingness of buyers to purchase them
core_image: 清晨的集市街：木棚下摆着成筐的果子，一杆秤搁在摊边，买主与卖主在摊前讨价
scene: 天刚亮，街边木棚下摆满果筐，买卖双方在摊前讨价。Growers bring their produce to a market where buyers bargain over each crate.
sceneCN: 前半情境：天刚亮，街边木棚下摆满果筐，买卖双方在摊前讨价；句中的 market 指「买卖双方定期相聚的集市场地」（第 1 个义项：作为交易场所的集市）。图中可辨识物件：木棚、果筐、杆秤、写价的木牌；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 市场；集市；交易领域；销路；股市；买方群体
行销；推销；把产品推向市场

senses.title: A place where buyers and sellers meet
senses.titleCN: 买卖双方相聚的集市场地
senses.definition: an open place, often with stalls, where people regularly come together to buy and sell goods
senses.definitionCN: 常设有摊位的露天场所，人们定期在此相聚买卖货物
senses.example: Farmers set up stalls at the weekly market.
senses.exampleCN: 农民每周在集市上摆摊。
senses.why: the Latin noun mercatus named the place and the trading done there, so the word began as a location for exchange.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 mercatus 既指场所也指在那里进行的交易，因此这个词最初就是交换的地点。

senses.title: Trade in one particular commodity
senses.titleCN: 某一种商品的交易领域
senses.definition: the whole body of buying and selling in one commodity or one sector, wherever it happens
senses.definitionCN: 某一种商品或某一部门中全部买卖活动的总和，不论发生在何处
senses.example: The world market for copper tightened last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年世界铜的交易领域收紧了。
senses.why: the place sense was transferred from a square to a field of trade, so that copper can have a market with no square at all.
senses.whyCN: 场所义从一方广场转移到一片交易领域，于是铜可以有市场，而完全不需要广场。

senses.title: Demand for a product
senses.definition: the number of buyers willing to purchase something, or the absence of such buyers
senses.definitionCN: 愿意购买某物的买者数量，或这类买者的缺乏
senses.example: There is little market for hand-written ledgers now.
senses.exampleCN: 如今手写账簿已没什么销路。
senses.why: without buyers a place of exchange is empty, so the word came to mean the willingness to buy rather than the ground it stands on.
senses.whyCN: 没有买主，交换的场所就是空的，于是这个词转而指购买的意愿，而不是它所在的那块地。

senses.title: The market for shares and securities
senses.definition: the organized exchange on which shares, bonds and currencies are traded, or trading there as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 买卖股票、债券与货币的有组织的交易所，或该处的交易整体
senses.example: Share prices fell across the market before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 午前整个股市的股价都下跌了。
senses.why: a stock exchange is a marketplace in the original sense, only with paper claims instead of crates, so the old word was kept.
senses.whyCN: 证券交易所就是原义上的集市，只是货物换成了纸面权益，旧词因此被沿用。

senses.title: Offered for sale
senses.titleCN: 在售；待售（置于售卖状态）
senses.definition: the state of being available to buy, as in a house that has come onto the market
senses.definitionCN: 处于可供购买的状态，如已挂牌出售的房子
senses.example: The building came onto the market in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼在春天挂牌出售。
senses.why: being placed before buyers is the modern equivalent of being carried to the stalls, and the phrase on the market keeps that image.
senses.whyCN: 被摆到买主面前，相当于旧时把货物挑到摊位上，这一短语保留了那个画面。

senses.title: To sell and promote a product
senses.definition: to promote and sell a product by choosing its buyers, its price and the way it is presented
senses.definitionCN: 通过选择买主、定价与呈现方式来推销并卖出产品
senses.example: The firm markets its software to schools.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把软件行销给学校。
senses.why: if a market is where goods find buyers, then to market is to do the work of bringing goods and buyers together.
senses.whyCN: 如果市场是货物找到买主的地方，那么行销就是把货物与买主带到一起的工作。

senses.title: The mechanism that sets prices
senses.definition: the system in which prices and quantities are settled by the competing decisions of many buyers and sellers
senses.definitionCN: 价格与数量由众多买卖双方的竞争性决定来敲定的系统
senses.example: The market, not the ministry, decides which suppliers survive.
senses.exampleCN: 决定哪些供应商存活的是市场，而不是部委。
senses.why: abstracting the place away leaves only its function: bringing competing offers together until a price emerges.
senses.whyCN: 把场所抽掉，只剩它的功能：把互相竞争的报价汇集起来，直到价格出现。

senses.title: The body of intended buyers
senses.definition: the group of people or institutions a seller intends to reach, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 卖方打算触及的那一群人或机构，被作为一个整体来看
senses.example: The brand's market is young urban readers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌的目标买方群体是年轻的城市读者。
senses.why: a seller who studies the crowd at the stalls ends by treating that crowd as an object to be served, which is the marketing sense.
senses.whyCN: 研究摊位前人群的卖方，最终把那群人当作服务对象，这就是营销义。

intro.en: Market is Latin in origin, not a native English word: it goes back to Latin mercatus 'market, trading', a noun from the verb mercari 'to trade', which in turn rests on merx (genitive mercis) 'goods'. It reached Old English through Old Northern French and Germanic channels. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: market 是拉丁来源，而非英语本族词：它上溯至拉丁名词 mercatus「市场、集市、交易」，该名词出自动词 mercari「做买卖」，而动词又基于 merx（属格 mercis）「货物」。它经古北法语与日耳曼中介进入古英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Merx, genitive mercis, meant 'goods, merchandise'. Its own deeper origin is uncertain, and no pre-Latin source can be demonstrated.
items.cn: merx（属格 mercis）意为「货物、商品」。它自身更深的来源不确定，无法证明任何拉丁语之前的源头。

items.en: From the noun came the deponent verb mercari 'to buy and sell, to trade', which names the activity rather than the goods.
items.cn: 由这个名词产生异态动词 mercari「买卖、做交易」，命名的是活动而非货物。

items.en: The noun mercatus 'market, marketplace, trading' was formed on the same stem, so place and activity were one word from the start.
items.cn: 名词 mercatus「市场、集市、交易」由同一词干构成，因此场所与活动从一开始就是一个词。

items.en: The form market is generally thought to have come to England through Old Northern French, with Germanic channels also involved in its spread.
items.cn: 一般认为 market 这一形式经古北法语传入英格兰，其传播也涉及日耳曼中介。

items.en: Old English already had market as a loanword, which is why the word counts as Latin in origin rather than as an inherited native term.
items.cn: 古英语已经以借词形式拥有 market，因此这个词算作拉丁来源，而非承继的本族词。

items.en: From the physical fair the word widened to trade in one commodity, to demand, to the share market and finally to the verb for promoting goods.
items.cn: 从有形的集市出发，这个词扩展到单一商品的交易、需求、股票市场，最后扩展到推销货物的动词义。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin root, so their kinship is real and can be traced; group two holds near neighbours that all name places or gatherings for trade.
note.cn: 第一组的词同出拉丁词根，亲缘关系真实可溯；第二组是同样指交易场所或聚会的近邻词。

entries.definition: Through Old French from Latin mercari: a person who trades, so it shares the root for 'goods' with market and adds an agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 经古法语来自拉丁 mercari：做买卖的人，与本词同出「货物」这一词根，只多了一个施事后缀。

entries.definition: From merx 'goods' through Old French: the goods themselves, which is the root meaning in concrete form.
entries.definitionCN: 经古法语来自 merx「货物」：货物本身，正是该词根的具体形态。

entries.definition: From Italian mercante, from Latin mercari: relating to trade, a later borrowing of the same root rather than a new coinage.
entries.definitionCN: 经意大利语来自拉丁 mercari：关于贸易的，是同一词根的后期借入，而非新造词。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus merx: trade viewed as an organized exchange between parties, another descendant of the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示「共同」的前缀加 merx：把贸易看作各方之间有组织的交换，是同一词根的另一支后裔。

entries.definition: Market plus place: the square or platform where trading happens, narrower than market because it has no demand or share-price senses.
entries.definitionCN: 由 market 与表示「地方」的成分复合而成：发生交易的广场或平台，比本词窄，因为不含需求与股价等义。

entries.definition: From Latin feria 'holiday': a periodic, often seasonal gathering for trade, with none of the abstract economic senses of market.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 feria「节日」：定期、常为季节性的交易聚会，不含本词那些抽象经济义。

entries.definition: From Persian through Turkish: a covered street of shops, a place word only and never a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 经土耳其语来自波斯语：有顶棚的店铺街，只作场所词，从不用作动词。

entries.definition: A shortened form of market kept for names and poetry; it retains only the place sense.
entries.definitionCN: market 的缩略形式，多用于名称与诗歌，只保留场所义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives rather than invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The chain runs goods, then trade, then place: merx, mercari, mercatus.
normal.cn: 链条是货物、交易、场所：merx、mercari、mercatus。

normal.en: The family runs market, marketing, marketplace, marketer, marketable, marketization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 market、marketing、marketplace、marketer、marketable、marketization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases separate the senses: on the market, market share, market forces, stock market.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分开各个义项：在售、市场份额、市场力量、股票市场。

normal.en: The same root shows in merchant, merchandise, mercantile and commerce.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 merchant、merchandise、mercantile 与 commerce 中。

normal.en: The verb takes an object: to market a product, and the -ing form is the noun marketing.
normal.cn: 动词要带宾语：把产品行销出去，其动名词形式就是名词「营销」。

abstract.en: Picture a square that is crowded at dawn and swept clean by noon.
abstract.cn: 想象一方广场，黎明时挤满人，到正午已被扫空。

abstract.en: Picture two columns on a page: what buyers want, and what they will pay.
abstract.cn: 想象纸页上两栏：买主想要什么，愿意付多少。

abstract.en: Picture a board of share prices where one company's fate becomes a single flashing number.
abstract.cn: 想象一块股价牌，一家公司的命运变成一个闪动的数字。

examples.en: The fishing market opens before sunrise and is empty by noon.
examples.cn: 鱼市在日出前开张，到正午便空了。

examples.en: A product with no market cannot survive, however carefully it is made.
examples.cn: 无论做得多用心，没有销路的产品都活不下去。

examples.en: The cooperative markets its coffee directly to roasters abroad.
examples.cn: 这家合作社把咖啡直接行销给国外的烘焙商。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马克」的谐音——集市上每件货物都用马克笔标上价钱 → 市场

root: 拉丁 merx（属格 mercis）「货物」→ 动词 mercari「做买卖」→ 名词 mercatus「市场、集市、交易」→ 经古北法语与日耳曼中介借入古英语 market；merx 更深来源不确定，故为拉丁来源而非英语本族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one building: goods (merx) are traded (mercari) in a place (mercatus). From the dawn square the line moves to trade in a single commodity, to the demand that fills or empties the square, to the share market that inherited the name, to the state of being offered for sale, to the verb that brings goods and buyers together, to the price-setting mechanism abstracted from the square, and finally to the crowd of buyers a seller sets out to serve.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一座建筑展开：货物在某个场所里被交易。从黎明时的广场出发，这条线依次走向单一商品的交易、决定广场空与满的需求、继承了这个名称的股票市场、被摆出来售卖的状态、把货物与买主带到一起的动词、从广场抽象出来的定价机制，最后走向卖方打算服务的那群买主。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dawn market square where crates change hands and the crowd thins by noon.
core.cn: 核心意象：黎明的集市广场，成筐货物易手，到正午人群渐散。

branches.en: PLACE AND COMMODITY: a square for exchange becomes a field of trade in one good.
branches.cn: 场所与商品：用于交换的广场变成某一种商品的交易领域。

branches.en: DEMAND AND SHARES: buyers make the square alive, and paper claims inherit its name.
branches.cn: 需求与证券：买主让广场有生气，纸面权益则继承了它的名称。

branches.en: OFFER AND PROMOTE: goods are placed before buyers, and someone must bring them there.
branches.cn: 摆出与推销：货物被摆到买主面前，而总得有人把它们带到那里。

branches.en: ALLOCATION: strip away the square and what remains is a mechanism that settles prices.
branches.cn: 配置：把广场抽走，剩下的就是一个敲定价格的机制。

branches.en: BUYER GROUP: the crowd at the stalls becomes the audience a seller intends to reach.
branches.cn: 买方群体：摊位前的人群变成卖方打算触及的对象。

intro.en: The word is a Latin root for 'goods' dressed in noun and verb endings, with English suffixes building the modern family on top.
intro.cn: 这个词是「货物」这一拉丁词根加上名词与动词词尾，再由英语后缀在其上搭起现代词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin merx and its verb mercari supply the stem; mercatus, the noun of place and activity, is the direct ancestor of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 merx 及其动词 mercari 提供词干；指场所与活动的名词 mercatus 则是英语这个词的直接祖先。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of goods in every member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根为词族中每个成员提供「货物」这一观念。

items.example: Merx names what is carried to the stalls.
items.exampleCN: merx 指被挑到摊位上的东西。

items.structure: mercari, mercatus sum (Latin deponent verb, first conjugation)
items.meaning: to trade, to buy and sell
items.example: The verb turns goods into an activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把货物变成一种活动。

items.example: The noun carries both the place and the dealing.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时承载场所与交易。

items.meaning: a place or system of exchange
items.example: Old English already used the borrowed noun.
items.exampleCN: 古英语已经使用这个借入的名词。

items.example: The compound keeps only the place sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词只保留场所义。

items.example: Marketing grew out of the verb to market.
items.exampleCN: 营销由动词「行销」发展而来。

items.meaning: the process or activity of doing
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a trade activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成一种行业活动。

items.example: Only marketable varieties reached the stalls.
items.exampleCN: 只有可销售的品种被送上摊位。

items.example: The suffix marks what can be sold.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出能够被卖出之物。

latinEntries.structure: mercari, mercatus sum (deponent verb, first conjugation)
latinEntries.meaning: to trade, to buy and sell

definition_zh: 两个人依法律或习俗结成的夫妻关系，也指确立这种关系的婚礼
definition_en: the legally or socially recognized union of two people as spouses, and the ceremony that establishes it
core_image: 一张铺着红纸的桌上并排放着两只旧戒指、一份证书和一把新房钥匙
scene: 老屋的堂屋里点着两支红烛，墙上贴着一张写满吉利话的纸。Her grandparents' marriage began with a ceremony that lasted three days.
sceneCN: 这里 marriage 指「两人依俗结成的夫妻结合」（第 1 个义项：由仪式与公认确立的配偶关系）；句意为她祖父母的婚姻始于一场持续三天的婚礼。可辨识物件：红烛、喜字、戒指、证书、钥匙；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: The recognized union of spouses
senses.titleCN: 被法律或社会承认的夫妻结合
senses.definition: the state in which two people are legally or socially recognized as spouses
senses.definitionCN: 两个人被法律或社会承认为配偶的状态
senses.example: Their marriage was registered at the county office in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的婚姻是春天在县里登记的。
senses.why: from Latin maritus 'husband', the noun names the wedded state itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自拉丁 maritus「丈夫」，直接指已婚状态本身。

senses.title: The wedding ceremony itself
senses.definition: the event in which vows are exchanged and the union is publicly made
senses.definitionCN: 交换誓言并公开确立结合的那场活动
senses.example: The whole village came to the marriage and stayed for the feast.
senses.exampleCN: 全村人都来参加婚礼，并留下来吃喜宴。
senses.why: the event and the state share one word because the rite is what creates the relation.
senses.whyCN: 仪式与状态共用一个词，因为正是仪式造成了这层关系。

senses.title: The ongoing state of being wed
senses.definition: the daily condition of living as a married couple over many years
senses.definitionCN: 多年来作为夫妻共同生活的日常状态
senses.example: Thirty years of marriage had taught them how to argue without wounding.
senses.exampleCN: 三十年的婚姻教会他们如何争吵却不伤人。
senses.why: the noun covers duration, not only the moment of union.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词涵盖持续时间，而不只是结合的那一刻。

senses.title: A type of marriage system
senses.definition: a socially defined form such as monogamy or polygyny, studied as a rule of the group
senses.definitionCN: 如一夫一妻或一夫多妻这类被社会定义的制度，作为群体规则来研究
senses.example: The community practiced marriage between cross-cousins.
senses.exampleCN: 这个社群实行交叉表亲之间的婚姻。
senses.why: societies classify forms of union, and the same noun labels the type.
senses.whyCN: 社会会给结合形式分类，同一个名词也就用来指类型。

senses.title: A close alliance between things
senses.titleCN: 事物之间的紧密结合（比喻义）
senses.definition: a metaphor for two different elements joined so closely that neither keeps its old shape
senses.definitionCN: 比喻两种不同成分紧密结合，彼此都不再保持原样
senses.example: The album is a marriage of folk melody and electronic rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 这张专辑是民歌曲调与电子节奏的结合。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the core idea of two parties becoming one.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了「两方成为一体」的核心意思。

senses.title: A card game of matching pairs
senses.definition: a card game in which players collect matching pairs, named after the paired union
senses.definitionCN: 玩家收集同名对子的一种纸牌游戏，因配对而成名
senses.example: The old men played marriage beside the stove all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 老人们整晚在炉边玩配对纸牌。
senses.why: the game is named for the matched pair, echoing the union sense.
senses.whyCN: 这种游戏因成对的牌而得名，与「结合」义呼应。

senses.title: A religious sacrament
senses.definition: the union regarded as a sacred vow rather than only a civil contract
senses.definitionCN: 被视为神圣誓约、而非仅是民事契约的结合
senses.example: The church treats marriage as a vow made before God.
senses.exampleCN: 教会把婚姻视为在神面前立下的誓约。
senses.why: religions read the union as sacred, adding a layer the law does not supply.
senses.whyCN: 宗教把这种结合读作神圣的，添加了法律不提供的一层。

senses.title: A political alliance between families
senses.definition: a union arranged to bind two families, courts or states rather than two individuals
senses.definitionCN: 为联结两个家族、宫廷或国家而非两个个人而安排的婚姻
senses.example: The treaty was sealed by a marriage between the two courts.
senses.exampleCN: 条约由两个宫廷之间的联姻加以巩固。
senses.why: kinship was once a diplomatic instrument, and the noun named that instrument.
senses.whyCN: 亲属关系曾是外交工具，这个词就指那件工具。

senses.title: The legal registration of the union
senses.titleCN: 婚姻的法律登记与效力
senses.definition: the recorded act that gives the union standing in courts and in inheritance law
senses.definitionCN: 使这种结合在法院与继承法中生效的登记行为
senses.example: Without registration, the marriage had no standing in court.
senses.exampleCN: 没有登记，这段婚姻在法庭上不具效力。
senses.why: modern states turn the relation into a recorded fact with legal consequences.
senses.whyCN: 现代国家把这种关系变成一项带有法律后果的登记事实。

intro.en: Marriage reaches English through Old French mariage from Latin maritare 'to wed', a verb built on maritus 'husband'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: marriage 经古法语 mariage 来自拉丁 maritare「使成婚」，该动词由 maritus「丈夫」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Maritus meant 'husband, married man', with the feminine marita 'wife'. Its deeper origin is uncertain: the link to mas 'male' is often proposed but not demonstrated.
items.cn: maritus 意为「丈夫、已婚男子」，阴性形式为 marita「妻子」。其更深来源不确定：把它与 mas「男性」联系起来是常见假说，但未获证实。

items.en: Maritare meant 'to wed, to give in marriage', and was also used of joining a vine to a supporting tree, an image of two lives bound together.
items.cn: maritare 意为「使成婚、嫁娶」，也用于把葡萄藤接到支撑的树上，暗含两条生命被绑在一起。

items.en: Old French mariage named both the wedded state and the wedding feast, and carried both senses into English in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 mariage 同时指已婚状态与婚宴，并在十三世纪把这两个义项带入英语。

items.en: English marriage kept the double sense from the start, so the same word names the relation and the day that begins it.
items.cn: 英语 marriage 从一开始就保留双重含义，同一个词既指关系，也指开启关系的那一天。

items.en: Canon law made marriage one of the sacraments, while civil law made it a contract with property consequences; both uses shaped the modern word.
items.cn: 教会法把婚姻列为圣事之一，世俗法则把它变成带有财产后果的契约；两种用法共同塑造了现代词义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): no convincing Latin derivation of maritus has been established, and the recorded first uses of the card-game sense are not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：maritus 尚无令人信服的拉丁派生来源；纸牌游戏义的最早书证年代也不固定。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin stock; group two holds near synonyms for the union or the event.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一拉丁词干的词；第二组是表示结合或仪式的近义词。

entries.definition: To take as a spouse or to join two people as spouses; marriage is the resulting state or event.
entries.definitionCN: 指娶、嫁或为两人证婚；marriage 是由此形成的状态或事件。

entries.definition: Of or relating to marriage, used in legal and medical contexts rather than in everyday talk.
entries.definitionCN: 指与婚姻有关的形容词，多用于法律与医学语境，而非日常口语。

entries.definition: A formal or religious word for the married state, felt as more solemn than marriage.
entries.definitionCN: 指已婚状态正式或宗教性的说法，比 marriage 更显庄重。

entries.definition: An old borrowing of the same French word, later displaced by marriage; it survives only in historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 同一法语词的古老借形，后来被 marriage 取代，只在历史文献中留存。

entries.definition: The ceremony and its celebration, without saying anything about the years that follow.
entries.definitionCN: 只指仪式及其庆祝，不涉及婚后的岁月。

entries.definition: A general word for two things becoming one, used of states, trade bodies and couples alike.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指两物合而为一，国家、工会与伴侣都可使用。

entries.definition: A formal, often journalistic word for a wedding, always plural and slightly ornamental.
entries.definitionCN: 指婚礼的正式用语，常见于报道，总是复数且略带修饰色彩。

entries.definition: A lasting arrangement between two people or firms; it makes no claim about vows or law.
entries.definitionCN: 指两人或两家公司之间的长期安排，不涉及誓言或法律。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: maritus meant husband, and -age turns the person into the state: the husband-state, then the union.
normal.cn: maritus 指丈夫，-age 把人变成状态：先是「丈夫的身份」，再是婚姻。

normal.en: The family runs marry, marriage, marital, premarital, extramarital and marriageable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 marry、marriage、marital、premarital、extramarital 与 marriageable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: arranged marriage, marriage vows, marriage license, marriage of convenience.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：包办婚姻、结婚誓言、结婚证书、权宜婚姻。

normal.en: The metaphor is alive in phrases like a marriage of flavours or a marriage of styles.
normal.cn: 比喻义仍活跃，如风味的结合、风格的结合。

normal.en: The card game sense survives in regional play and in dictionaries, not in general speech.
normal.cn: 纸牌义仍留在地方玩法与词典中，日常口语已不常用。

abstract.en: Picture two streams meeting and then sharing one bed.
abstract.cn: 想象两条溪流汇合后共用一条河床。

abstract.en: Picture a knot tied in public and carried privately for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一个当众打好的结，被私人携带多年。

abstract.en: Picture a vine grafted onto a tree so that both keep growing.
abstract.cn: 想象一根藤接到树上，两者都继续生长。

examples.en: The law recognizes a marriage only after both parties sign the register.
examples.cn: 法律只有在双方签署登记簿后才承认婚姻。

examples.en: Their marriage survived drought, debt and two long separations.
examples.cn: 他们的婚姻熬过了干旱、债务与两次长期分离。

examples.en: Critics called the novel a marriage of detective plot and family saga.
examples.cn: 评论家称这部小说是侦探情节与家族史诗的结合。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「marry（结婚）+ age（年龄）」——到了年纪就结婚

root: 拉丁 maritus「丈夫」（阴性 marita「妻子」）→ 动词 maritare「使成婚」→ 古法语 mariage → 英语 marriage。maritus 的更深来源不确定，与 mas「男性」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one bond: two people are joined, and the joining is then read as an event, a daily state, a social rule, a metaphor, a game, a sacrament, a treaty and a register entry.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个结合展开：两个人被连在一起，这个结合再依次被读作事件、日常状态、社会制度、比喻、游戏、圣事、盟约与登记记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rings set side by side on one sheet of paper, neither complete without the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两枚戒指并排放在同一张纸上，缺一枚都不成双。

branches.en: THE BOND AND ITS RECORD: the relation comes first, and the register is how a state sees it.
branches.cn: 结合与记录：关系在先，登记则是国家看见它的方式。

branches.en: THE DAY AND THE VOW: a public rite turns a private promise into a recognised union.
branches.cn: 那一天与那誓言：公开仪式把私下承诺变成被承认的结合。

branches.en: THE LONG MIDDLE: most of a marriage is neither the wedding nor the law but ordinary duration.
branches.cn: 漫长的中间段：婚姻的大部分既不是婚礼也不是法律，而是平常的持续。

branches.en: RULES AND ALLIANCES: a group can define the form, and families can use it as a treaty.
branches.cn: 规则与联盟：群体可以规定形式，家族也可以把它当作条约。

branches.en: TWO BECOME ONE: the metaphor and the card game both play on the matched pair.
branches.cn: 合二为一：比喻义与纸牌义都借成对之物做文章。

intro.en: Marriage is a Latin noun stem plus a French ending, and the same stem builds the legal, medical and everyday words around it.
intro.cn: marriage 由一个拉丁名词词干加一个法语词尾构成，同一词干还构成它周围的法律、医学与日常用词。

latinIntro.en: Latin maritus and marita sit behind marriage, marry and marital; the ending -age names a state or a collection.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 maritus 与 marita 是 marriage、marry 与 marital 的来源；词尾 -age 表状态或集合。

items.example: Maritus supplied the whole family of words.
items.exampleCN: maritus 提供了整个词族的来源。

items.example: The feminine form fills out the pair.
items.exampleCN: 阴性形式补全了这一对。

items.structure: maritare, maritavi, maritatum (Latin verb, first conjugation)
items.example: The verb could also mean to join a vine to a tree.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也可指把藤接到树上。

items.example: The suffix turns the act of wedding into a lasting state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把成婚之举变成持续状态。

items.example: Old French kept both senses in one word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语用一个词保留了这两个义项。

items.example: English kept the double sense intact.
items.exampleCN: 英语完整保留了这双重含义。

items.example: Marry is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: marry 是名词背后的动词。

items.meaning: relating to a husband or to marriage
items.example: Marital law speaks of duties between spouses.
items.exampleCN: 婚姻法讲的是配偶之间的义务。

items.example: Premarital agreements are signed before the wedding.
items.exampleCN: 婚前协议在婚礼之前签署。

items.example: Extramarital adds the idea of crossing a boundary.
items.exampleCN: extramarital 增添了越界的意思。

definition_zh: 结婚；嫁；娶；为……主持婚礼；使紧密结合
definition_en: to become someone's husband or wife, to take a particular person as a spouse, to conduct a wedding ceremony for a couple, or to join two things closely together
core_image: 两个人把各自的一只手放进同一只手里，一条线从此牵住两端
scene: 秋天的礼堂门口，两家人并肩站着，等那扇木门打开。Her grandmother married a fisherman from the next village in the spring of that hard year.
sceneCN: 这里 marry 是「嫁、娶」，指与某人结成夫妻（第 1 个义项：两个人成为丈夫与妻子）；句意为那年艰难岁月的春天，她的祖母嫁给了邻村的一位渔民。图中可辨识物件：礼堂木门、并肩的两家人、等候的人群。

pos.zh: 结婚；嫁；娶；为……主持婚礼；使紧密结合

collocations.zh: 把技巧与耐心结合起来

derivatives.zh: 由古法语 mariage 而来，与 marry 同出一源，义为「婚姻；婚礼」
出自拉丁语 maritalis（婚姻的），与 marry 同源，义为「婚姻的；夫妻的」
由 marriage 加表示「可以……的」后缀 -able 构成，义为「到了可以结婚的年龄的」
由表示否定的前缀 un- 加 married 构成，义为「未婚的」

senses.title: To become husband and wife
senses.definition: to become the husband or wife of another person, or to have a wedding with someone
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人成为夫妻，或与某人举行婚礼
senses.example: They married in a small church near the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一座靠海的小教堂里结了婚。
senses.why: Latin maritus named a married man and maritare named the act of taking a spouse, so the verb begins as the name of a public bond, not of a private feeling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 maritus 指已婚的男子，动词 maritare 指娶妻或嫁人，所以这个词从一开始就是那层公开缔结的关系的名字，而不是某种私人心情。

senses.title: To take a particular person as a spouse
senses.definition: to take someone as your husband or wife, used when the partner is named as the object
senses.definitionCN: 把某个人娶为妻或嫁为夫，通常把配偶直接放在动词后面
senses.example: She married a fisherman who had never left the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 她嫁给了一个从未离开过这片海湾的渔民。
senses.why: Because the partner is the direct object, English can say who was chosen; that is why it says marry someone and not marry with someone, unlike many European languages.
senses.whyCN: 因为配偶直接做了宾语，英语就能说出被选中的人是谁；所以它说 marry someone，而不像许多欧洲语言那样加一个表示「和」的介词。

senses.title: To conduct a wedding ceremony
senses.definition: of a priest, registrar or other official, to perform the ceremony that makes two people husband and wife
senses.definitionCN: 指神职人员、登记官员或别的主持人举行仪式，使两个人成为夫妻
senses.example: The old priest had married half the couples in that valley.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老神父为山谷里半数的新人主持过婚礼。
senses.why: The same verb serves the couple and the person who declares them married, because a wedding needs an authorized voice to announce that the bond is now in force.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词既用于新人，也用于那个宣布他们成婚的人，因为婚礼需要一把被授权的嗓子说出这层关系已经生效。

senses.title: To join two things closely
senses.titleCN: 使紧密结合；使融为一体
senses.definition: to bring two things together so that they work as a single whole, said of ideas, skills or flavours
senses.definitionCN: 把两样东西凑在一起，使它们像一体那样运作，多用于想法、技艺或味道
senses.example: The chef marries smoke and citrus in a single spoonful.
senses.exampleCN: 这位厨师把烟熏味与柑橘味融进同一勺里。
senses.why: A marriage is a lasting union, so the verb stretches that image to anything deliberately put into a lasting pair, from a sauce to two crafts practised together.
senses.whyCN: 婚姻是一种长久的联合，于是这个动词把这幅画面推到任何被有意配成一对的东西上，从一味酱汁到两门一起做的手艺。

intro.en: Marry came into English from Old French in the thirteenth century, and behind it stands a Latin word for a married man; the word has always been about a bond made in public, not about romance.
intro.cn: marry 在十三世纪经古法语进入英语，背后是拉丁语里表示「已婚男子」的词；它从出现起讲的就是公开缔结的关系，而不是浪漫。

items.en: Maritus was the ordinary Latin noun for a husband and could also be an adjective for what belongs to a married man; it supplied the base of the verb.
items.cn: maritus 是拉丁语里表示丈夫的普通名词，也可作形容词指属于已婚男子的，并成为那个动词的词基。

items.en: Maritare meant to give a woman in marriage or to take a spouse, and it treated the wedding as a legal and social act rather than a mood.
items.cn: maritare 意为把女子嫁出或娶一位配偶，它把婚礼当作一件法律与社会的行为，而不是一种情绪。

items.en: Old French marier carried the same sense and supplied the form English borrowed, and its noun mariage came along with it.
items.cn: 古法语 marier 保留同样的意思，提供了英语借入的词形，名词 mariage 也随着一起传来。

items.en: Spellings such as marien and maryen settled into marry, and the verb took both the partner and the officiating priest as its object.
items.cn: marien、maryen 这类拼写后来固定为 marry，动词的宾语既可以是配偶，也可以是主持婚礼的神职人员。

items.en: Modern English keeps the wedding sense, allows both marry someone and get married, and stretches the verb to any close pairing such as flavours or skills.
items.cn: 现代英语保留婚礼义，允许 marry someone 与 get married 两种说法，并把动词延伸到任何紧密的配对，例如两种味道或两门技艺。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the wedding family and the Latin words behind it; the near group gathers verbs and nouns for taking a partner or joining two things.
note.cn: 形近组收与婚礼同族的词以及它背后的拉丁词；近义组收表示结为伴侣或把两样东西合起来的动词与名词。

entries.definition: The state or ceremony of being husband and wife, from Old French mariage.
entries.definitionCN: 夫妻的状态或婚礼；出自古法语 mariage，与 marry 同族。

entries.definition: Having a husband or wife, formed from marry with -ed.
entries.definitionCN: 有丈夫或妻子的；已婚的；由 marry 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: Relating to marriage or to a husband, from Latin maritalis.
entries.definitionCN: 与婚姻或丈夫有关的；出自拉丁语 maritalis，与 marry 同源。

entries.definition: Not having a husband or wife, formed with the negative prefix un-.
entries.definitionCN: 没有丈夫或妻子的；未婚的；由否定前缀 un- 加 married 构成。

entries.definition: To take someone as a husband or wife, or to perform a wedding; chiefly literary and older use.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人娶为妻或嫁为夫，或主持婚礼；多用于文学与较早的用法。

entries.definition: To marry someone, or to support and adopt a belief; from Latin sponsus, a promised spouse.
entries.definitionCN: 与某人结婚；也指支持并采纳某种主张；出自拉丁语 sponsus（订婚者）。

entries.definition: Two people who are married or in a romantic relationship, or to join two things together.
entries.definitionCN: 已婚或相恋的两个人；也指把两样东西连接起来。

entries.definition: To join two people or things so that they become one.
entries.definitionCN: 把两个人或两样东西结合起来，使它们成为一体。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin noun for a married man, and its family keeps returning to the wedding, the spouse, and the lasting pair.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「已婚男子」的名词上，它的同族词反复回到婚礼、配偶与长久的一对。

normal.en: Latin maritus means a husband, so marry starts as a word about a public bond rather than a private feeling.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 maritus 意为丈夫，所以 marry 起点是一层公开的关系，而不是私人的心情。

normal.en: The verb maritare meant to give a bride or take a spouse, and English borrowed its French descendant marier.
normal.cn: 动词 maritare 意为把新娘嫁出或娶一位配偶，英语借入的是它的法语后代 marier。

normal.en: Because the partner is the direct object, English says marry someone; adding with would make it sound like a ceremony you both merely attend.
normal.cn: 因为配偶是直接宾语，英语说 marry someone；如果加一个表示「和」的介词，听起来就像一场你们只是出席的仪式。

normal.en: The priest who marries a couple uses the same word from the opposite side: he is the one who makes the bond official.
normal.cn: 为一对新人主持婚礼的神父从相反的一侧用同一个词：他是让这层关系正式生效的人。

normal.en: Marriage, marital and married all go back to the same Latin base, one as the noun, one as an adjective of the husband, one as a state.
normal.cn: marriage、marital 与 married 都回到同一个拉丁词基，一个作名词，一个作丈夫的形容词，一个表示所处的状态。

abstract.en: Two hands closing on each other, and the word names the closing, not the warmth that led to it.
abstract.cn: 两只手彼此握住，而这个词命名的是握住本身，不是通向它的那点温热。

abstract.en: A wedding is a sentence said aloud in front of witnesses, and marry is that sentence turned into a verb.
abstract.cn: 婚礼是一句在证人面前说出口的话，而 marry 就是那句话变成的动词。

abstract.en: Once a bond can be made official, it can be made between flavours or skills, and the old public vow quietly becomes a cook's trick.
abstract.cn: 一旦一种结合可以被正式认定，它也能在味道或技艺之间成立，旧日的公开誓言便悄悄变成了厨子的手法。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a bond publicly made; the senses then divide into the wedding itself, the named partner, the official who declares it, and any close pairing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一层公开缔结的关系；义项由此分成婚礼本身、被点明的配偶、宣布礼成的主持人，以及任何紧密的配对。

definition_zh: 极好的；了不起的；令人惊叹的；奇妙的；（旧）奇迹般的
definition_en: extremely good and enjoyable, so beautiful or strange that it fills the mind with wonder, or, in older use, brought about by something beyond nature
core_image: 一个孩子抬头看天，忽然铺开的绿光让他张着嘴说不出话
scene: 北境旅店的门口，旅客们裹着厚外套抬头看天，绿色的光带正从山脊后面漫上来。The whole sky turned marvelous for a few minutes, then faded to plain dark.
sceneCN: 这里 marvelous 是「令人惊叹的、奇妙的」，指好到让人说不出话（第 2 个义项：因超出想象而使人惊叹）；句意为整片天空奇妙的模样只维持了几分钟，随后又归于平淡的暗色。图中可辨识物件：旅店门口、厚外套、山脊后的绿光带。

pos.zh: 极好的；令人惊叹的；奇迹般的

derivatives.zh: 出自古法语 merveille（奇迹），是 marvelous 的词根名词，义为「奇迹；令人惊叹的事物」
由 marvelous 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「极好地；令人惊叹地」
由 marvelous 加表示性质的名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「奇妙；令人惊叹的性质」

senses.title: Extremely good and enjoyable
senses.definition: very good, pleasant or impressive, used in ordinary speech about things people enjoy
senses.definitionCN: 非常好、令人愉快或令人印象深刻，日常口语中用来夸人喜欢的事物
senses.example: We had a marvelous evening on the rooftop.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在屋顶上度过了一个极好的夜晚。
senses.why: Mirabilia named wonderful things, and everyday speech wore the sense down from causing wonder to plain very good, exactly as great and terrific slid from awe into approval.
senses.whyCN: mirabilia 原本指令人惊叹的事物，日常口语把这层意思从「引起惊叹」磨成了简单的「很好」，就像 great 与 terrific 也都从敬畏滑向了赞许。

senses.title: So beautiful or strange that the mind stops
senses.definition: so beautiful, strange or unlikely that it makes you stop and wonder at it
senses.definitionCN: 美、奇或不合常理到让人停下来发怔
senses.example: A marvelous green light spread over the ridge and would not fade.
senses.exampleCN: 一道奇妙的绿光铺过山脊，久久不散。
senses.why: Before it was praise, the word pointed at whatever mirari means to wonder at; that older sense survives whenever the thing itself, and not the pleasure, is what astonishes.
senses.whyCN: 在变成一句称赞之前，这个词指向 mirari（惊奇地看）所面对的东西；当令人吃惊的是事物本身而不是愉快感受时，这层较旧的意思就还活着。

senses.title: Brought about beyond the course of nature, an older use
senses.titleCN: 奇迹般的；超自然的（旧用法）
senses.definition: of an event, produced by a power outside the ordinary course of nature, a sense common in older religious writing
senses.definitionCN: 指某件事由自然常规之外的力量造成，这一义项多见于较早的宗教文字
senses.example: The old chronicle calls the healing marvelous rather than medical.
senses.exampleCN: 那部旧编年史记述这次痊愈为奇迹，而非医术。
senses.why: Mirabilis could describe what only a miracle explains, so the adjective kept a doorway to the supernatural long after it had learned to mean merely excellent.
senses.whyCN: mirabilis 可以形容只有神迹才解释得通的事，所以这个形容词在学会表示「很好」之后，仍长期保留着一扇通向超自然的门。

intro.en: Marvelous goes back to a Latin verb for wondering, through a noun for wonderful things, and it reached English by way of Old French with a noun and an adjective travelling together.
intro.cn: marvelous 可以追到拉丁语里表示「惊奇地看」的动词，中间经过一个指「奇妙之事」的名词，再随名词与形容词一同经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Mirari meant to wonder at something, and its forms gave the whole family the idea of being looked at with astonishment.
items.cn: mirari 意为对某物感到惊奇，它的各种形式把「被惊讶地注视」这一观念给了整族词。

items.en: Mirabilis, wonderful or astonishing, described anything that provoked that look, from a strange animal to an unexpected healing.
items.cn: mirabilis 意为奇妙的、惊人的，用来描述任何引起那种注视的东西，从一只怪异的动物到一次意外的痊愈。

items.en: The neuter plural mirabilia meant wonderful things, and in that plural form it named the wonders collected in writing and in talk.
items.cn: 中性复数 mirabilia 意为「奇妙之事」，正是这个复数形式用来指被写进书里、说在口中的种种奇观。

items.en: Old French turned mirabilia into merveille, a wonder or marvel, and built the adjective merveillos on the same stem.
items.cn: 古法语把 mirabilia 变成 merveille，意为奇迹、奇观，并在同一词干上造出形容词 merveillos。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective as marvellous, the British spelling, and American usage later wrote marvelous; the noun marvel came from the same French word.
items.cn: 英语把形容词借作 marvellous，即英式拼写，美式用法后来写作 marvelous；名词 marvel 也出自同一个法语词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun and the two spellings built on the Latin stem for wonder; the near group gathers other adjectives of praise and amazement.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「惊奇」词干上的名词与两种拼写；近义组收其他表示称赞与惊异的形容词。

entries.definition: A wonderful or astonishing thing, or to feel wonder at it.
entries.definitionCN: 令人惊叹的事物；也指对之感到惊奇；与 marvelous 出自同一个古法语词。

entries.definition: The British spelling of marvelous, with exactly the same senses.
entries.definitionCN: marvelous 的英式拼写，义项完全相同。

entries.definition: To regard someone or something with respect and warm approval, from Latin admirari built on mirari.
entries.definitionCN: 带着敬意与赞赏看待某人某物；出自拉丁语 admirari，其词基正是 mirari。

entries.definition: An extraordinary event that natural laws cannot explain, from Latin miraculum.
entries.definitionCN: 无法用自然规律解释的非凡事件；出自拉丁语 miraculum，与 marvelous 同源。

entries.definition: Extremely good, or filling you with wonder.
entries.definitionCN: 极好的；或使人充满惊叹的。

entries.definition: Extremely good, or so strange that it seems imagined.
entries.definitionCN: 极好的；或奇到仿佛想象出来的。

entries.definition: So surprising that it is hard to believe.
entries.definitionCN: 令人吃惊到难以相信的。

entries.definition: Of the very highest quality.
entries.definitionCN: 质量极高的；卓越的。

normalIntro.en: The word grows out of a Latin verb for staring in astonishment, and its family keeps returning to wonder, the thing that causes it, and praise worn smooth by daily use.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语表示「惊奇地看」的动词长出来，它的同族词反复回到惊奇、引起惊奇的事物，以及被日常使用磨滑的称赞。

normal.en: Wonder is the seed: Latin mirari means to stare in astonishment, and mirabilis names whatever makes you stare.
normal.cn: 惊奇是种子：拉丁语 mirari 意为惊奇地看，mirabilis 则命名任何让你看住不动的东西。

normal.en: Mirabilia, wonderful things, passed into Old French merveille and gave English both marvel and the adjective marvellous.
normal.cn: mirabilia 意为奇妙之事，传进古法语成为 merveille，并给英语留下 marvel 与形容词 marvellous。

normal.en: The British spelling keeps the double l of the French ending, while American usage writes marvelous with a single l.
normal.cn: 英式拼写保留法语词尾的双写 l，美式用法则把 marvelous 写成单写 l。

normal.en: Admire and miracle sit on the same Latin root, one naming the look you give, the other naming the event that earns it.
normal.cn: admire 与 miracle 站在同一个拉丁词根上，一个命名你给出的目光，一个命名赢得这目光的事件。

normal.en: The everyday sense of very good came later, when speakers spent a word of wonder as ordinary praise, as they did with terrific and fabulous.
normal.cn: 口语里「很好」的意思来得较晚，说话人把一个表示惊奇的字当普通称赞花出去，就像 terrific 与 fabulous 那样。

abstract.en: A child under a suddenly lit sky: the word begins in the open mouth, not in the judgement.
abstract.cn: 一个站在骤然亮起的天空下的孩子：这个词起于张开的口，不起于评判。

abstract.en: Praise is a fossil of awe; every cheap marvelous was once a genuine astonishment.
abstract.cn: 称赞是敬畏的化石；每一句廉价的 marvelous 都曾经是一次真心的惊奇。

abstract.en: Two l's or one, the same Latin wonder is still shut inside the word.
abstract.cn: 双写 l 也好，单写 l 也好，同一个拉丁语的惊奇仍被关在词里。

examples.en: We had a marvelous evening on the rooftop.
examples.cn: 我们在屋顶上度过了一个极好的夜晚。

examples.en: A marvelous green light spread over the ridge and would not fade.
examples.cn: 一道奇妙的绿光铺过山脊，久久不散。

examples.en: The old chronicle calls the healing marvelous rather than medical.
examples.cn: 那部旧编年史记述这次痊愈为奇迹，而非医术。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马佛勒斯」——马看见佛光铺满天空，惊讶得说不出话；记住 marvelous 是奇妙的、极好的。

root: 拉丁语 mirari（惊奇地看）→ mirabilis（奇妙的）→ 中性复数 mirabilia（奇妙之事）→ 古法语 merveille（奇迹）与 merveillos（奇妙的）→ 英语 marvel 与 marvelous；美式拼写省去一个 l。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the look of astonishment; the senses then divide into worn-down praise, the thing that truly amazes, and the older claim that something lies beyond nature.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是那副惊讶的目光；义项由此分成被磨平的称赞、真正令人惊异的事物，以及较早的「超出自然」之说。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child looking up at a sky suddenly filled with green light, mouth open, saying nothing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个孩子抬头看见天空忽然铺满绿光，张着嘴说不出话。

branches.en: a rooftop evening praised long after it ends
branches.cn: 屋顶的夜晚，结束后仍被反复称赞

branches.en: green light climbing over a dark ridge
branches.cn: 绿光爬上黑暗的山脊

branches.en: a chronicle calling a healing a wonder
branches.cn: 编年史把一次痊愈记作奇迹

branches.en: a crowd kneeling before a cure no doctor explains
branches.cn: 众人跪在医生解释不了的痊愈前

branches.en: a traveller telling the same story twice
branches.cn: 旅人把同一个故事讲了两遍

intro.en: A Latin verb for wondering, its adjective, the plural noun for wonders, two French forms and one English suffix hold the word together.
intro.cn: 一个表示惊奇的拉丁动词、它的形容词、指奇妙之事的名词复数、两个法语形式与一个英语后缀，把这个词撑在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin mirari, mirabilis and mirabilia are recorded and reliable; Old French merveille and merveillos are the accepted bridge to English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mirari、mirabilis 与 mirabilia 有记录且可靠；古法语 merveille 与 merveillos 是被认可的进入英语的桥梁。

definition_zh: 面具；面罩；口罩；掩饰；伪装；遮住；掩盖
definition_en: a covering worn over the face for disguise, performance or protection, a pad worn over the nose and mouth against infection, a false appearance that hides feelings, or to cover and conceal something
core_image: 一只手把一张薄薄的面具举到脸前，镜中人立刻换上了另一副表情
scene: 剧场后台的镜子前，演员把一张纸浆面具举到脸前，试着调整角度。Behind the curtain a dozen dancers were adjusting masks of painted silk.
sceneCN: 这里 mask 是「面具」（第 1 个义项：罩在脸上用来伪装或表演的覆盖物）；句意为幕布后面，十来个舞者正在调整绘着花纹的丝质面具。图中可辨识物件：后台镜子、纸浆面具、幕布、丝质面具。

pos.zh: 面具；面罩；口罩；掩饰；伪装

derivatives.zh: 由 mask 加 -ed 构成，义为「戴面具的；蒙面的」
由 mask 加 -ing 构成，义为「遮盖；掩蔽」
由表示相反动作的前缀 un- 加 mask 构成，义为「揭下面具；揭露真面目」
经法语 mascarade 借入，与 mask 同出意大利语 maschera 一族，义为「假面舞会；伪装」

senses.title: A covering worn over the face
senses.definition: an object worn over the face to hide it, to frighten, or to protect it
senses.definitionCN: 罩在脸上用来遮住面孔、吓人或保护面孔的物件
senses.example: The actor held a paper mask up to the mirror.
senses.exampleCN: 演员把一张纸面具举到镜子前。
senses.why: The word reached English from the theatre, where a mask changes who the wearer appears to be, so the covering and the new face arrive in one object.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是从剧场进入英语的，在那里一张面具会改变戴者看起来是谁；遮盖与换脸因此是同一件东西的两面。

senses.title: A pad worn over the nose and mouth against infection
senses.definition: a piece of cloth or paper worn over the nose and mouth to filter air and reduce the spread of germs
senses.definitionCN: 罩在口鼻上、用来过滤空气并减少病菌传播的布片或纸片
senses.example: Every nurse in the ward wore a fresh mask for each shift.
senses.exampleCN: 病房里每位护士每班都换一只新口罩。
senses.why: Protection is the other half of the theatre sense: the same covering that hides a face can also stand between a face and what floats in the air.
senses.whyCN: 保护是剧场那层意思的另一半：同一张遮盖物既能把脸藏起来，也能把脸与空气里飘着的东西隔开。

senses.title: A false appearance that hides what a person feels
senses.definition: a way of behaving that hides true feelings or intentions from other people
senses.definitionCN: 一种把真实情绪或意图挡在别人视线之外的表现方式
senses.example: His cheerful mask slipped the moment the door closed.
senses.exampleCN: 门一关上，他那副快活的面具就掉了。
senses.why: If a mask can hand you another face, then a manner put on for other people is a mask in the same sense, and the word moves from pasteboard to behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 既然一张面具能给你换上另一张脸，那么为别人摆出的姿态就是同一意义上的面具，词义便从纸板走到了举止。

senses.title: To cover the face with a mask
senses.definition: to put a mask on someone or on your own face, or to cover a face in a picture
senses.definitionCN: 给某人或自己戴上面具，或在图像里把脸部遮住
senses.example: The dancers masked themselves before the curtain rose.
senses.exampleCN: 幕布升起前，舞者们给自己戴上了面具。
senses.why: Once the noun names the object, the verb is simply the act of putting it on, and English routinely turns a covering into the gesture that applies it.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦指那件东西，动词就只是把它戴上去的动作；英语常把一件遮盖物直接变成施加它的那个手势。

senses.title: To hide or keep something from being noticed
senses.definition: to conceal a feeling, a sound, a taste or a fact so that other people do not notice it
senses.definitionCN: 把情绪、声音、味道或事实藏起来，让别人察觉不到
senses.example: The engine's hum masked the noise of the door opening.
senses.exampleCN: 引擎的嗡鸣盖住了门被推开的声音。
senses.why: Anything laid over a surface hides what is under it, so the word for a face covering extends to smells, sounds and facts that something else has covered.
senses.whyCN: 凡是铺在表面上的东西都会遮住下面的事物，于是「遮脸之物」这个词也推到被别的东西盖住的气味、声音与事实。

intro.en: Mask is a word of uncertain origin that came to English through French and Italian theatre, and even its earliest recorded Latin form has no settled source.
intro.cn: mask 是一个来源不确定的词，经法语与意大利语剧场传入英语，连它有记录的最早拉丁形式也没有定论。

items.en: The earliest documented link is Medieval Latin masca, a word for a mask or a terrifying spectre; its own origin is uncertain and may lie outside Latin altogether.
items.cn: 有记录的最早环节是中古拉丁语 masca，指面具或骇人的幽灵；它本身的来源不确定，甚至可能根本不在拉丁语之内。

items.en: Italian maschera named the mask worn in street theatre and carnival, and the word travelled with touring performers.
items.cn: 意大利语 maschera 指街头戏剧与狂欢节上戴的面具，这个词随巡回演出的艺人一起流传。

items.en: French took it as masque, meaning both the mask itself and the masked entertainment staged at court.
items.cn: 法语借作 masque，既指面具本身，也指宫廷里演的假面娱乐。

items.en: Middle English maske named a covering for the face and a disguise, and the spelling settled as mask in modern English.
items.cn: 中古英语 maske 指遮脸之物与伪装，现代英语里拼写固定为 mask。

items.en: Modern English keeps the theatre mask, adds the protective mask of medicine and industry, and uses the verb for hiding feelings, sounds and facts.
items.cn: 现代英语保留戏剧面具，又加上医学与工业上的防护面罩，并用动词表示掩盖情绪、声音与事实。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derivatives and the theatrical relatives of the word; the near group gathers other coverings and verbs of hiding.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词的派生词与戏剧上的同族词；近义组收其他遮盖物以及表示隐藏的动词。

entries.definition: Wearing a mask, or hidden from view, formed from mask with -ed.
entries.definitionCN: 戴着面具的；被遮住看不见的；由 mask 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: To remove someone's mask, or to reveal what they really are.
entries.definitionCN: 揭下某人的面具；揭露其真面目；由 un- 加 mask 构成。

entries.definition: A party where people wear masks and costumes, or a pretence kept up in public.
entries.definitionCN: 人们戴面具、穿戏服的舞会；也指在众人面前维持的伪装；与 mask 同出意大利语 maschera 一族。

entries.definition: A courtly entertainment with music, dancing and masks, popular in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
entries.definitionCN: 十六、十七世纪流行的宫廷娱乐，含音乐、舞蹈与面具；与 mask 同出法语 masque。

entries.definition: A change of appearance or manner meant to hide who you are.
entries.definitionCN: 为隐藏身份而改变外貌或举止；伪装。

entries.definition: A piece of thin cloth worn over the face or head, or anything that hides something.
entries.definitionCN: 罩在脸上或头上的薄布；也指任何遮蔽物。

entries.definition: To place something over another thing so that it cannot be seen.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物盖在另一物上，使它看不见。

entries.definition: To hide something or keep it from being known.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物藏起来，或使它不为人知。

normalIntro.en: The word came in with masked players rather than with doctors, and its family keeps returning to the changed face, the barrier and the thing hidden underneath.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是随戴面具的演员而不是医生进入英语的，它的同族词反复回到换过的脸、那道屏障，以及被遮在下面的东西。

normal.en: The record starts with Medieval Latin masca, a mask or a spectre, and even that word's origin is uncertain.
normal.cn: 记录从中古拉丁语 masca 开始，指面具或幽灵，而连这个词的来源都不确定。

normal.en: Italian maschera belonged to carnival and street theatre, so the English word arrived with performers rather than with physicians.
normal.cn: 意大利语 maschera 属于狂欢节与街头戏剧，所以这个词是随演员而不是随医生来到英语的。

normal.en: Unmask is simply un- plus mask, the gesture of taking the covering off, and therefore of showing the truth.
normal.cn: unmask 就是 un- 加 mask，即把遮盖物取下来的动作，因此也就是把真相露出来。

normal.en: The medical mask keeps the object and changes the purpose, from hiding a face to shielding one.
normal.cn: 医用口罩留着同一件东西，却换了目的，从把脸藏起来变成把脸护起来。

normal.en: The verb mask works on sounds and facts as easily as on faces, because anything laid over a surface hides what lies beneath.
normal.cn: 动词 mask 用在声音与事实上和用在脸上一样顺手，因为任何铺在表面上的东西都会遮住下面的内容。

abstract.en: A second face held in one hand: the word never quite separates covering from pretending.
abstract.cn: 一张被单手举着的第二张脸：这个词始终没能把遮盖与假装彻底分开。

abstract.en: The same paper square can hide a robber or protect a nurse, and the word does not care which.
abstract.cn: 同一方纸片既能遮住强盗，也能护住护士，而这个词并不在意是哪一种。

abstract.en: What masks a sound also masks a fact, and a theatre trick becomes an ordinary verb.
abstract.cn: 能盖住声音的东西也能盖住事实，一个舞台把戏就这样变成了寻常动词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a covering held in front of the face; the senses then divide into performance, protection, a front put on for others, the act of putting it on, and anything that hides what lies beneath.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是举在脸前的一件遮盖物；义项由此分成表演、防护、为别人摆出的门面、戴上它的动作，以及任何遮住下方事物的东西。

definition_zh: 团块；大量、大批；质量；群众、大众；弥撒；聚集、集结
definition_en: a large shapeless body of matter, a great quantity of it, or the amount of matter in a body
core_image: 一盆揉好的面团被两只手按下去，整团摊在案板上，越揉越沉
scene: 面粉加水和成一大团，摊在案板上占了半张台面，两只手按下去要费点力。A mass of dough filled the whole board.
sceneCN: 这里 mass 指没有定形、聚成整体的一大团东西（第 1 个义项：不分形状的团块）；句意：一大团面团占满了整块案板。图中可辨识物件：面团、案板、面粉袋、擀面杖；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 团块；大量；质量；群众；弥撒

forms.label: 单数（物质义通常不可数）

senses.title: A shapeless lump
senses.definition: a body of matter with no clear shape, often formed by pressing things together
senses.definitionCN: 没有明确形状的一团物质，常由挤压而成
senses.example: A mass of dough filled the whole board.
senses.exampleCN: 一大团面团占满了整块案板。
senses.why: Latin massa meant a lump of dough or metal, so the shapeless lump is the root picture of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 massa 指面团或金属的一团，因此「无定形的一团」是这个词的根源画面。

senses.title: A very large quantity
senses.definition: a great number or amount of things taken together
senses.definitionCN: 许多事物合在一起所形成的大数量
senses.example: A mass of evidence supports the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 大量证据支持这一主张。
senses.why: a lump is many small pieces pressed into one, so the word naturally shifted from one lump to a heap of things.
senses.whyCN: 一团是许多小块压在一起，于是这个词自然从「一团」滑到「一堆」。

senses.title: Quantity of matter in physics
senses.definition: the quantity of matter in a body, measured by its resistance to acceleration
senses.definitionCN: 物体所含物质的量，以其抵抗加速度的程度来量度
senses.example: Mass is not the same as weight, though scales blur the two.
senses.exampleCN: 质量与重量并不相同，尽管秤常把两者混在一起。
senses.why: physicists needed a word for how much stuff a body contains, and the lump word was the obvious choice.
senses.whyCN: 物理学家需要指称一个物体含有多少实体，那团东西的词自然是首选。

senses.title: The common people
senses.definition: the ordinary people of a society, considered as one body
senses.definitionCN: 社会中的普通人，被当作一个整体来看
senses.example: The reform was popular with the masses but not with the owners.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革受大众欢迎，却不受业主欢迎。
senses.why: crowds pressed together in a square look like one lump, and politics named that lump the masses.
senses.whyCN: 广场上挤在一起的人群看上去就是一团，政治语言把这团叫作「大众」。

senses.title: The religious service
senses.definition: the central service of the Roman Catholic Church, especially one said for the dead
senses.definitionCN: 罗马天主教会的主要礼仪，尤指为亡者举行的那一场
senses.example: They attended early Mass on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们星期天参加了清早的弥撒。
senses.why: this sense comes from Latin missa 'dismissal', a different source from massa, and must never be merged with the lump word.
senses.whyCN: 这一义出自拉丁 missa「遣散」，与 massa 不同源，绝不能与「团块」那个词混为一谈。

senses.title: To gather in a crowd
senses.definition: to come together in large numbers, as troops or protesters do
senses.definitionCN: 以大量人数聚拢，如军队或抗议者
senses.example: Troops massed along the border overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 部队一夜之间集结在边境一带。
senses.why: if a mass is many units pressed into one body, then to mass is the act of pressing them together.
senses.whyCN: 既然 mass 是许多单位压成一个整体，那么动词 mass 就是把它们压到一起的动作。

senses.title: Large-scale, for everyone
senses.definition: produced or done on a large scale and aimed at ordinary people
senses.definitionCN: 以大规模制作或进行、面向普通人的
senses.example: Mass production brought the clock within reach of clerks.
senses.exampleCN: 大批量生产让职员也买得起钟表。
senses.why: the adjective turns the lump into a scale word: one lump, then one industry serving a whole market.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把「一团」变成尺度词：先是一团，再是整个服务一方市场的产业。

senses.title: The bulk or greater part
senses.definition: the greater part of something, considered as one undifferentiated body
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的较大部分，被看作一个未加区分的整体
senses.example: The mass of the population lives along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 人口的大部分住在沿海一带。
senses.why: a lump is undivided, so the word also covers the majority when nobody bothers to split it up.
senses.whyCN: 一团是不加分割的，因此当没人去细分时，这个词也指「大多数」。

intro.en: Mass in the sense of a lump comes from Latin massa, generally thought to come from Greek maza 'barley cake'. The church sense comes from Latin missa 'dismissal' and is a separate word.
intro.cn: 「团块」义的 mass 来自拉丁 massa，一般认为源自希腊 maza「大麦饼」；弥撒义来自拉丁 missa「遣散」，是另一个词。

items.en: Maza meant a barley cake or a lump of kneaded dough, and it is generally thought to be the older source behind Latin massa.
items.cn: maza 指大麦饼或揉成团的面，一般认为它是拉丁 massa 更早的来源。

items.en: Massa meant a lump, a mass of metal or dough; the further link to Greek maza is a common view rather than a documented chain.
items.cn: massa 指一团、一块金属或面团；它与希腊 maza 的联系是常见看法，而非有文献可查的链条。

items.en: Missa meant 'dismissal' and became the name of the church service; it has nothing to do with massa and must be kept apart.
items.cn: missa 意为「遣散」，后来成为礼拜仪式的名称；它与 massa 毫无关系，必须分开。

items.en: Both words entered English in the Middle Ages, the lump word through French and the church word through the liturgy.
items.cn: 两个词都在中世纪进入英语：团块义经法语而来，礼仪义经教会用语而来。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the lump word was narrowed by physics to the measurable quantity of matter in a body.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，物理学把「团块」词收窄为物体中可量度的物质的量。

items.en: The first dates for the political and industrial senses are approximate; both words are well attested from the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 政治义与工业义的最早年代为约数；两个词在中世纪都已有充分书证。

note.en: The first group holds forms built on massa plus two near-forms, one of which is famously a different word; the second group holds quantity words.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 massa 的词形，另加一个形近但著名地属于另一个词的词；第二组是表示数量的词。

entries.definition: Built on mass with an adjective suffix, meaning 'huge and solid'; it describes the lump rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 在 mass 上加形容词后缀构成，意为「巨大而结实的」；它描述那团东西而不命名它。

entries.definition: A compact group of mountains, from French massif and the same massa stock; it is a shaped lump of rock.
entries.definitionCN: 指紧凑的一群山，出自法语 massif 与同一 massa 词源；它是被塑造过的一团岩石。

entries.definition: From French amasser, built on masse; to heap things into one lump, usually wealth or evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 出自法语 amasser，由 masse 构成；把东西堆成一团，通常指财富或证据。

entries.definition: The volume or the greater part of something; mass stresses the stuff, bulk stresses the size it takes up.
entries.definitionCN: 指体积或较大部分；mass 强调那团实体，bulk 强调它占的空间。

entries.definition: A pile of separate things stacked up; a mass can be one continuous body, a heap is always many pieces.
entries.definitionCN: 分开的东西堆成一摞；mass 可以是一个连续的整体，heap 永远是许多件。

entries.definition: A large number of people gathered together; the phrase for the masses is a political body, not a crowd in a street.
entries.definitionCN: 聚在一起的一大群人；「大众」是政治意义上的整体，不是街上的一群人。

entries.definition: The force of gravity on a body; mass is how much matter it holds, weight is how hard gravity pulls it.
entries.definitionCN: 重力对物体施加的力；mass 是所含物质的量，weight 是重力拉它的力度。

entries.definition: More than half of a counted group; the bulk phrase means an unsplit body, not a tally.
entries.definitionCN: 被计数群体中过半的部分；而「人口的大部分」是不加细分的整体，不是点数结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin source, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁来源、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin massa was a lump of dough, so mass begins as a shapeless lump.
normal.cn: 拉丁 massa 是一团面，因此 mass 最初就是无定形的一团。

normal.en: The family runs mass, massive, massively, massless and biomass.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mass、massive、massively、massless 与 biomass。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale sense: mass media, mass production, mass market.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出规模义：大众传媒、大批量生产、大众市场。

normal.en: Physics pairs mass with weight, and the two are not interchangeable.
normal.cn: 物理把 mass 与 weight 配对，二者不能互换。

normal.en: Remember that Mass the service comes from Latin missa, not from massa.
normal.cn: 要记住弥撒义的 Mass 出自拉丁 missa，而非 massa。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd in a square pressing into one single dark shape from above.
abstract.cn: 从高处看，广场上的人群挤成一个黑色整体。

abstract.en: Picture a snowball rolling downhill and growing heavier with every turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一个雪球滚下山坡，每转一圈就更沉一些。

abstract.en: Picture a baker's hands pushing a whole table of dough into one lump.
abstract.cn: 想象面包师把整张台面的面按成一团。

examples.en: The nebula contains a mass of gas several times that of the sun.
examples.cn: 这团星云所含气体的质量是太阳的若干倍。

examples.en: Mass tourism has changed the old harbour beyond recognition.
examples.cn: 大众旅游把这个老港口改变得面目全非。

examples.en: Protesters massed outside the hall before the vote.
examples.cn: 表决之前，抗议者在大厅外集结。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马死」——一大群马挤成一团，马死了也堆成一大堆 → 团块、大量

root: 希腊 maza「大麦饼、面团」→ 拉丁 massa「一团、一块」→ 法语 masse → 英语 mass「团块、大量」；物理学再收窄为「质量」；弥撒义的 Mass 另出拉丁 missa「遣散」，与此无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all begin with one lump: dough on a board, a heap of evidence, a measured quantity in physics, a crowd pressed into one body, the bulk of a population, the act of pressing a crowd together, an industry serving everyone, and an unsplit majority.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一团东西出发：案板上的面团、一堆证据、物理里可量度的量、挤成一个整体的人群、人口的大部分、把人挤到一起的动作、服务所有人的产业，以及不加细分的多数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lump of dough pressed flat across a whole board.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团面被按平，摊满整块案板。

branches.en: THE LUMP AND THE HEAP: one continuous body first, then many pieces pressed into a great quantity.
branches.cn: 一团与一堆：先是连续的一体，再是许多件压成大数量。

branches.en: THE MEASURED LUMP: physics turns the lump into a number that resists acceleration.
branches.cn: 可量度的团：物理学把这团东西变成一个抵抗加速度的数。

branches.en: PEOPLE AS ONE BODY: a crowd pressed together becomes the masses, and an unsplit bulk becomes the majority.
branches.cn: 被当作一体的民众：挤在一起的人群成为大众，未加细分的整体成为多数。

branches.en: THE OTHER WORD: the church service sounds the same but descends from missa, a root of its own.
branches.cn: 另一个词：宗教礼仪读音相同，却出自 missa，自有一个词根。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE SCALE: pressing things together, and an industry that serves a whole market.
branches.cn: 动作与尺度：把东西压到一起，以及服务整个市场的产业。

intro.en: Mass is a Latin noun of a lump, with a small English family built on it; the church word Mass is a separate stock and is marked as such.
intro.cn: mass 是拉丁语里表示「一团」的名词，英语在其上长出一个不大的词族；弥撒义的 Mass 另有来源，下面单独标出。

latinIntro.en: Latin massa gives mass, massive, massif and amass through French; missa is a different Latin noun and gives only the church sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 massa 经法语给出 mass、massive、massif 与 amass；missa 是另一个拉丁名词，只给出礼仪义。

items.meaning: lump; mass of metal or dough
items.meaningCN: 一团；金属或面团的一块
items.example: The root supplies the picture of a shapeless lump.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「无定形一团」的画面。

items.example: One word covers the lump, the heap and the measured quantity.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词兼指团块、堆与可量度的量。

items.example: A massive wall is one great lump of stone.
items.exampleCN: 一堵厚墙就是一大团石头。

items.example: The massif rises as one block from the plain.
items.exampleCN: 那片山地从平原上整块隆起。

items.example: To amass is to press many things into one heap.
items.exampleCN: amass 就是把许多东西压成一堆。

items.meaning: the total living matter in an area
items.meaningCN: 某一区域内的生物总量
items.example: The prefix narrows the lump to living stuff.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把这团东西限定为活物。

items.example: The compound turns the lump into a sales scale.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把「一团」变成销售的尺度。

items.structure: Latin noun, first declension, separate source
items.example: This root is not related to massa in any way.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根与 massa 没有任何关系。

definition_zh: 巨大的；沉重的；大量的；严重的；体格魁梧的；块状的（岩体）；大面积的（病变）；厚重的（建筑）
definition_en: very large in size, weight or amount, often so large that it is striking or hard to deal with
core_image: 港口边立着一整块从山体切下的石料，旁边的卡车小得像个玩具
scene: 港口入口立着一整块从山体切下的石料，旁边的卡车小得像个玩具。A massive block of granite now stands at the harbour entrance.
sceneCN: 这里指体积巨大、分量惊人（第 1 个义项：形体或体量极大）；句意为一块巨大的花岗岩石料如今立在港口入口处；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 直接来自拉丁 massa「团块」，是该形容词的词基，义为「团块；大量；群众的」
由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「巨大地；极其」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「巨大；沉重感」
由「团块」加表示动作或集合的名词后缀构成，义为「体量组合」，是建筑用语
由同一词根经法语进入英语，义为「山块；地块」，指连成整体的一组山体

senses.title: Very large in size
senses.definition: occupying far more space than ordinary objects of its kind, so that it dominates a view
senses.definitionCN: 占据的空间远大于同类常见物体，因而在视野中占主导
senses.example: A massive crane lifted the bridge section into place.
senses.exampleCN: 一台巨大的起重机把桥段吊装到位。
senses.why: The Latin noun meant a lump or a mass, so the adjective first describes sheer bulk.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词意为「团块、一堆」，因此这个形容词首先描述的是纯粹的体量。

senses.title: Heavy and solid
senses.definition: thick and weighty, made of material that feels hard to move
senses.definitionCN: 厚而重，由让人感到难以搬动的材料做成
senses.example: The altar is a massive slab of stone.
senses.exampleCN: 祭坛是一整块沉重的石板。
senses.why: A mass has weight as well as size, so the adjective carries both impressions at once.
senses.whyCN: 团块既有体积也有重量，因此这个形容词同时带着两种感受。

senses.title: Huge in amount
senses.definition: present in a very large quantity, said of data, sums, effort or numbers of people
senses.definitionCN: 以极大的数量存在，用于数据、金额、努力或人数
senses.example: The archive holds a massive amount of correspondence.
senses.exampleCN: 这间档案馆藏有大量往来信件。
senses.why: Amounts can pile up like material, and a heap that keeps growing becomes a mass.
senses.whyCN: 数量可以像材料一样堆积，越堆越高的那一堆就成了「团块」。

senses.title: Extremely serious in effect
senses.definition: very great in severity, so that recovery or repair is difficult
senses.definitionCN: 严重程度极大，以至于恢复或修复都很困难
senses.example: The earthquake caused massive damage to the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 地震给老城造成了严重破坏。
senses.why: Damage has size too, and damage of enormous size is expressed with the word for bulk.
senses.whyCN: 破坏也有「大小」，巨大规模的破坏就用表示体量的词来表达。

senses.title: Broad and heavy in build
senses.definition: having a large, solid body, said of a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 身体大而结实，用于人或动物
senses.example: A massive guard stood at the gate all night.
senses.exampleCN: 一名魁梧的守卫整夜站在门口。
senses.why: A body can have the same solid bulk as a stone block, and English applies the word to people.
senses.whyCN: 身体可以有和石块一样厚实的体量，英语便把这个词用在人身上。

senses.title: Formed as one unbroken rock body
senses.definition: in geology, said of rock that has no visible bedding or layering, appearing as one solid mass
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中用于看不出层理、呈一整块的岩石
senses.example: The cliff is cut into massive granite with no clear layers.
senses.exampleCN: 这面崖壁由无明显层理的整块花岗岩构成。
senses.why: Geology uses the word for rock that behaves as a single lump rather than as stacked sheets.
senses.whyCN: 地质学用这个词指表现得像一整块、而不是叠层薄片的岩石。

senses.title: Very extensive in medicine
senses.definition: said of a bleed, clot or infarct that covers a large part of an organ
senses.definitionCN: 用于覆盖器官很大一部分的出血、血栓或梗死
senses.example: He survived a massive heart attack last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 去年冬天他挺过了一次大面积心肌梗死。
senses.why: Clinical language measures lesions by extent, and an extent near the whole organ is massive.
senses.whyCN: 临床按范围量度病灶，范围接近整个器官的就称为「大面积」。

senses.title: Thick and plain in construction
senses.definition: built with heavy walls and simple, undecorated forms, often of stone
senses.definitionCN: 以厚重墙体与简洁无装饰的形式建造，常用石材
senses.example: The cathedral's massive walls were built to last centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这座主教座堂的厚重墙体是为挺过数百年而建的。
senses.why: Architecture judges weight and simplicity together, and a building that shows its mass is called massive.
senses.whyCN: 建筑把重量与简洁一起评价，一座显露自身质量的建筑就被称为「厚重」。

intro.en: Massive comes from Latin massa 'lump, mass', itself from Greek maza 'barley cake', through French massif. English adopted it in the sixteenth century, and geology, medicine and architecture later gave it precise uses.
intro.cn: massive 来自拉丁 massa「团块、一堆」，后者源于希腊 maza「大麦饼」，经法语 massif 进入英语，十六世纪被采用；地质、医学与建筑后来赋予它精确用法。

items.en: Maza named a kneaded barley cake, a single shapeless lump of dough, and the image of one solid mass began there.
items.cn: maza 指揉成的大麦饼，是一团没有形状的面团，「一整块实体」的画面由此开始。

items.en: Massa meant a lump, a mass or a body of material, and it also gave English mass.
items.cn: massa 意为团块、一堆或一团材料，也给出英语的 mass。

items.en: French massif described something solid and bulky, and English took the adjective in that form.
items.cn: 法语 massif 形容坚实而笨重的东西，英语照这个形式引入形容词。

items.en: English massive first described heavy objects and bodies, then extended to amounts and effects.
items.cn: 英语的这个词先形容沉重的物体与身体，后扩展到数量与后果。

items.en: Geology uses massive for rock without bedding, and architecture for walls that display their weight.
items.cn: 地质学用这个词指无层理的岩石，建筑用指显露自身重量的墙。

items.en: Clinical writing measures an infarct or bleed by how much of an organ it covers, and a very large one is massive.
items.cn: 临床文字按覆盖器官的多少来量度梗死或出血，覆盖很大的就称为大面积。

note.en: The first group shares the lump stem; the second group holds size words that differ in scale, shape or tone.
note.cn: 第一组共享「团块」词干；第二组是表示大小的词，在规模、形状或语气上各有不同。

entries.definition: A quantity of matter, or a large number of people; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 一定量的物质，或一大群人；是形容词背后的名词。

entries.definition: To an enormous degree; it often modifies verbs such as increase or build.
entries.definitionCN: 达到巨大程度；常修饰「增加」「建造」一类动词。

entries.definition: The quality of being huge and heavy; a state noun used in description.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大而沉重的性质；是用于描写的状态名词。

entries.definition: The arrangement of volumes in a building; an architectural term from the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑中各体量的组合；同一词干来的建筑术语。

entries.definition: Very big; the general word, without the suggestion of solid weight.
entries.definitionCN: 非常大；通用词，不带「坚实沉重」的暗示。

entries.definition: Extremely large; it stresses scale beyond expectation rather than mass.
entries.definitionCN: 极大；强调超出预期的规模，而非质量。

entries.definition: Large and awkward to move because of shape; it adds inconvenience to size.
entries.definitionCN: 因形状而大得难以搬动；在「大」之外多了不便。

entries.definition: Astonishingly large, as a giant statue; it carries awe rather than weight.
entries.definitionCN: 大到惊人，如巨型雕像；带惊叹意味，而非重量感。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means a lump: massive things come as one solid block.
normal.cn: 词根意为「团块」：巨大的东西是一整块实心的。

normal.en: The family runs mass, massively, massiveness and massing.
normal.cn: 同族词包括团块、巨大地、巨大、体量组合。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark quantity and severity: massive amount, massive damage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出数量与严重程度：大量、严重破坏。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark science: massive rock, massive heart attack.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出科学用法：块状岩体、大面积心肌梗死。

normal.en: Its neighbours differ: huge is general, bulky adds awkwardness, colossal adds awe.
normal.cn: 近邻有别：huge 是通用词，bulky 多了笨重，colossal 多了惊叹。

abstract.en: Picture a single stone so large that a road bends around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块大到公路要绕着走的石头。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd so thick that no one can cross it.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人多到没人能穿过去。

abstract.en: Picture a door whose frame alone weighs more than a car.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，光是门框就比一辆车重。

examples.en: The company made a massive investment in new machinery.
examples.cn: 这家公司在新机器上投入了巨额资金。

examples.en: A massive storm shut down every ferry in the region.
examples.cn: 一场猛烈的风暴让该地区所有渡轮停运。

examples.en: The cathedral's massive walls have stood for six hundred years.
examples.cn: 这座主教座堂厚重的墙已经立了六百年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马四伏」——四匹马伏在一起才拉得动，形容巨大沉重

root: 希腊 maza「大麦饼、一团面团」→ 拉丁 massa「团块」→ 法语 massif → 英语 massive；同族 mass、massif、massing。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe one solid bulk: an object in space, weight in the hand, a growing quantity, the scale of damage, a body, a rock body, a lesion, or a wall.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述同一团实在的体量：空间里的物体、手里的重量、不断增大的数量、破坏的规模、身体、岩体、病灶，或一堵墙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one shapeless lump so big that it dominates whatever stands beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一大团没有形状的实体，大到让它旁边的一切都显得渺小。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BASE: a large object and its solid weight.
branches.cn: 物理基础：庞大的物体与其坚实的重量。

branches.en: THE QUANTITATIVE FORM: a heap of data, money or people.
branches.cn: 数量形态：一堆数据、金钱或人。

branches.en: THE SEVERITY FORM: damage on a scale that is hard to repair.
branches.cn: 严重形态：难以修复的大规模破坏。

branches.en: THE HUMAN FORM: a broad, heavy body.
branches.cn: 人的形态：宽厚沉重的身体。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL FORMS: rock without bedding, a lesion covering much of an organ, and walls that show their weight.
branches.cn: 技术形态：无层理的岩体、覆盖器官大部的病灶，以及显露重量的墙。

intro.en: Massive rests on Latin massa 'lump' and the adjective ending -ive; English adds endings for manner, state and architectural arrangement.
intro.cn: massive 建立在拉丁 massa「团块」与形容词词尾 -ive 之上；英语再加表示方式、状态与建筑组合的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin massa 'lump' gives English mass directly; Medieval Latin massivus and French massif give the adjective massive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 massa「团块」直接给出英语 mass；中世纪拉丁 massivus 与法语 massif 给出形容词 massive。

items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的来源。

items.meaning: a body of matter; a great number
items.example: The noun kept both the physical and social senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时保留物理与社会两义。

items.example: The ending makes a describing word of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成描述词。

items.example: The medieval form passed through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个中世纪形式经法语传下。

items.example: English extended it to amounts and severity.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它扩展到数量与严重程度。

items.example: The suffix gives the degree adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀给出程度副词。

items.example: The suffix names the quality of bulk.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名「体量巨大」的性质。

items.example: The noun names a geological mass of rock.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名地质上的岩块。

items.example: The ending builds the architectural term massing.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出建筑术语「体量组合」。

items.example: The adverb modifies verbs of growth and spending.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词修饰「增长」「开支」类动词。

derivatives.zh: 直接来自拉丁 massa，义为「团块；大量」
由该形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「巨大地」
由该形容词加性质名词后缀构成，义为「巨大」
由词根加动作名词后缀构成，义为「体量组合」
由同一词根经法语进入英语，义为「山块」

definition_zh: 主人；硕士；大师；能手；精通；掌握；控制；制服
definition_en: a person who owns or has authority over something, an advanced university degree, an expert in a craft, or to learn and gain complete control of something
core_image: 老人一抬手，院子里的人和马都停下来等他的吩咐
scene: 旧宅的院子里，一位老人牵马走到廊下，抬手示意年轻仆人不必再跟着。The old master of the house knew every corner of the garden.
sceneCN: 这里 master 是「主人」（第 1 个义项：对一处宅院、牲畜或仆役拥有支配权的人）；句意为这座宅子的老主人熟悉园子的每一个角落。图中可辨识物件：廊下的马、抬手示意的老人、退后的仆人。

derivatives.zh: 由 master 加表示「状态、性质」的后缀 -y 构成，义为「精通；掌控」
由 master 加表示「充满……」的后缀 -ful 构成，义为「有掌控力的；技艺高超的」
由 master 与 piece 复合而成，本指学徒期满后用以证明手艺的作品，义为「杰作」
由 master 加 -ly 构成，义为「精巧的；显出大师手笔的」

senses.title: The owner or head of a household
senses.definition: a person who owns a house, an animal or a servant and has authority over them
senses.definitionCN: 对一处宅院、一头牲畜或一名仆役拥有所有权并有权支配的人
senses.example: The dog follows its master everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 这条狗到处跟着它的主人。
senses.why: Latin magister named the man who stood above others, and the first English uses kept that household power: the master is the one whose word is obeyed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 magister 指站在他人之上的人，英语最早的用法保留的正是这种宅院里的权力：主人就是话被听从的那一位。

senses.title: A holder of a master's degree
senses.definition: an advanced university degree below a doctorate, or the person who holds it
senses.definitionCN: 低于博士学位的大学高级学位，也指持有这一学位的人
senses.example: She took a master's degree in urban planning.
senses.exampleCN: 她取得了城市规划专业的硕士学位。
senses.why: In the medieval university the magister was the licensed teacher, so the title of the qualified teacher became the name of the highest taught degree.
senses.whyCN: 在中世纪的大学里，magister 是取得授课资格的老师，于是「合格教师」这个头衔后来成了最高的授课型学位之名。

senses.title: An expert in a craft or art
senses.definition: a person who is highly skilled in a craft, an art or a technique
senses.definitionCN: 在某门手艺、艺术或技艺上极为精湛的人
senses.example: The glass master shaped the bowl with three quick turns.
senses.exampleCN: 那位玻璃大师转了三下就把碗形定了下来。
senses.why: Because magister marked the person who had finished the whole training, skill itself came to be measured by the word: a master is the one at the top of the craft.
senses.whyCN: 因为 magister 标出的是完成了全部训练的人，技艺高低便用这个词来衡量：大师就是一门手艺里站在顶端的那一个。

senses.title: To learn or understand something completely
senses.definition: to learn a skill or subject so well that you can use it without effort
senses.definitionCN: 把一项技能或一门学问学到运用自如的程度
senses.example: He mastered the old engine by taking it apart twice.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那台旧发动机拆了两遍，就把它摸透了。
senses.why: The noun for a qualified teacher turned into a verb: to master a thing is to reach the level at which you could explain it to someone else.
senses.whyCN: 指「合格老师」的名词转成了动词：master 一样东西，就是达到能够把它讲给别人听的水平。

senses.title: To bring something under control
senses.definition: to gain control over a strong feeling, an animal or a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 把强烈的情绪、一头动物或困难的局面压住并置于掌控之下
senses.example: She mastered her anger before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 她先把怒气压住，才开口回答。
senses.why: If a master is the person who gives orders, the verb can also mean making a wild thing obey, and the object shifts from a skill to whatever refuses to be controlled.
senses.whyCN: 既然 master 是发号施令的人，动词也就表示让不听话的东西服从，宾语于是从一门技能转到任何不肯受控的对象。

intro.en: Master comes from Latin magister, the man with authority, and reached English through Old French; the word still carries both the power to command and the title of a qualified teacher.
intro.cn: master 出自拉丁语 magister（有权威的人），经古法语进入英语；这个词至今同时带着发号施令的权力与「合格教师」的头衔。

items.en: Magis is the Latin adverb for more or rather, and it marks the greater side of any comparison.
items.cn: magis 是拉丁语副词，意为「更多、更」，标出任何比较中更强的那一边。

items.en: Magister was built on magis with a comparative ending and named the man placed above others, above all the teacher in charge of pupils.
items.cn: magister 由 magis 加比较级词尾构成，指被置于他人之上的人，首先指管教学生的老师。

items.en: Old French kept the word as maistre, a lord, teacher or craftsman, and its spelling travelled into English with the Norman court.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词保留为 maistre，指领主、教师或匠人，它的拼写随诺曼宫廷传入英语。

items.en: Middle English master covered the head of a house, the qualified teacher and the skilled craftsman, and the universities gave it to a degree.
items.cn: 中古英语的 master 兼指一家之主、合格教师与熟练匠人，大学又把这个称号给了一个学位。

items.en: Modern English adds the verb to master, keeps the academic degree, and still uses the noun for an animal's owner and for a supreme practitioner.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了动词 master，保留了学位义，也仍用这个名词指动物的主人与某一行的顶尖高手。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives and Latin relatives of the word; the near group gathers names for owners, experts and the highly skilled.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词的派生词与拉丁同族词；近义组收表示主人、专家与高超技艺者的词。

entries.definitionCN: 对技能或学问的完全掌握；由 master 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: Showing great skill or firm control.
entries.definitionCN: 显出高超技艺或强力掌控的；由 master 加 -ful 构成。

entries.definitionCN: 带有权威气派的；也与地方法官有关；出自拉丁语 magister。

entries.definition: A public official who judges minor cases.
entries.definitionCN: 审理轻微案件的公职人员；词根同为拉丁语 magister。

entries.definition: A person with special knowledge or skill in a field.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一领域有专门知识或技能的人。

entries.definition: The person who legally possesses something.
entries.definitionCN: 合法拥有某物的人。

entries.definition: Very skilled at something.
entries.definitionCN: 在某事上很在行、很熟练的。

entries.definition: A performer with outstanding technical skill.
entries.definitionCN: 技艺出众的演奏者或表演者。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin adverb of comparison, and its family keeps returning to standing above others: as owner, as teacher, as expert, as full control.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语的一个比较副词上，它的同族词反复回到「站在他人之上」：作为主人、老师、能手，直到完全的掌控。

normal.en: Latin magis means more, and magister is the person who is more than the others, so the title began as a comparison.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 magis 意为「更多」，magister 就是「比别人更多」的那个人，所以这个头衔起初是一次比较。

normal.en: Old French maistre kept the meaning and lost some letters on the way to English master.
normal.cn: 古法语 maistre 保留了意思，在进入英语 master 的过程中丢掉了一些字母。

normal.en: Master's degree goes back to the medieval university, where a magister was a teacher licensed to lecture.
normal.cn: 硕士学位可以追到中世纪大学，那时 magister 是获准开讲的教师。

normal.en: Mastery adds -y for the state, masterful adds -ful for the quality, and both keep the sense of standing at the top.
normal.cn: mastery 加 -y 指状态，masterful 加 -ful 指性质，两者都保留着「站在顶端」的意思。

normal.en: Master a skill literally repeats the old teacher image: you learn a thing until you could teach it yourself.
normal.cn: master a skill 字面上重复了旧的教师形象：你学一样东西，直到能够自己去教它。

abstract.en: Authority is pictured as a raised hand: a house, a horse and a servant all wait for the same signal.
abstract.cn: 权威被想象成抬起的一只手：房子、马与仆人都等同一个示意。

abstract.en: A degree, a craft and a command share one word because all three are proofs that the training is finished.
abstract.cn: 学位、手艺与掌控共用一个词，因为三者都是「训练已经完成」的凭证。

abstract.en: The word began as a comparison and ended as a certificate, yet both still ask who stands higher.
abstract.cn: 这个词起于一次比较，落成一纸证书，可两者都仍在问：谁站得更高。

examples.en: The old master of the house knew every corner of the garden.
examples.cn: 这座宅子的老主人熟悉园子的每一个角落。

examples.en: He mastered the old engine by taking it apart twice.
examples.cn: 他把那台旧发动机拆了两遍，就把它摸透了。

examples.en: She took a master's degree in urban planning.
examples.cn: 她取得了城市规划专业的硕士学位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马斯特」——马背上坐得最稳的那个人被喊作斯特；记住 master 是主人，也是把本事练到顶的人。

root: 拉丁语 magis（更多、更）加比较级词尾构成 magister（更有权威的人、教师），经古法语 maistre 进入英语；同族词多与权威、教导和技艺高超有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person placed above others; the senses divide into the head of a household, the qualified teacher and the degree, the top craftsman, and the verb of reaching full command.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是站在他人之上的人；义项由此分成一家之主、合格教师与学位、顶尖匠人，以及达到完全掌控的动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old man raises one hand and the yard, the horse and the servants all wait for his word.
core.cn: 核心意象：老人一抬手，院子里的人、马和仆人都停下来等他的吩咐。

branches.cn: 主人归来时宅门前点起的灯

branches.en: a hood and gown on a graduation morning
branches.cn: 毕业清晨的方帽与长袍

branches.en: a glassblower's hands turning a bowl in three moves
branches.cn: 吹玻璃的人三下转出一只碗

branches.en: an engine taken apart and put back together
branches.cn: 拆开又装回的发动机

branches.en: a raised voice stopped before it leaves the mouth
branches.cn: 抬高的话音在出口之前被按住

intro.en: A Latin comparative adverb, its comparative noun, the French form of that noun and four English endings carry the word from a lord's hall to a workshop bench.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语比较副词、由它构成的比较级名词、这个名词的法语形式，再加四个英语词尾，把这个词从领主的厅堂带到工匠的台前。

latinIntro.en: Latin magis, more, and magister, the man who is more than others, are the reliable source of the family; Old French maistre is the form that English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 magis（更多）和 magister（比别人更多的那个人）是这个词族可靠的源头；英语借入的是古法语形式 maistre。
